     3	/-!
     4	# Diagonal branches of the coordinate strategies of the direct low-degree game
     5	
     6	The mature `j`-restricted diagonal sampler decodes to a direct direction with
     7	vanishing prefix below the reversed index `i = Fin.rev j`, and the transported
     8	question of `Transport.Questions` carries the leading index of that direction.
     9	On the generic event that the direction is nonzero at `i`, the leading index
    10	is `i` and the question is the canonical direct question of the direct sample
    11	`(p, i, v)`, where the mature defect is bounded by the direct rejection.
    12	Otherwise the restricted direction is also the restriction at the next index,
    13	so the mature quantity recurses to that index with the factor `q⁻¹`, the
    14	probability that the sampled coordinate vanishes; at the last index the zero
    15	direction has the last coordinate as its leading index by convention and no
    16	recursion occurs.  Summing the recursion shows that each mature diagonal
    17	branch is at most `q / (q - 1) ≤ 2` times the corresponding branch rejection
    18	of the direct game.  The factor is genuine: a strategy that answers the
    19	canonical question of a direction badly and the non-canonical questions of the
    20	same geometric line well has mature diagonal failure exceeding the direct
    21	branch rejection.
    22	
    23	## References
    24	
    25	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:214-458`
    26	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:49-65,130-151`
    27	- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-121`
    28	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    29	-/
    30

    40	/-! ## Direction coordinates and the one-coordinate recursion
    41	
    42	The mature `j`-restricted diagonal sampler decodes to a direct direction with
    43	vanishing prefix below the reversed index `i = Fin.rev j`, and the transported
    44	question carries the leading index of that direction.  On the generic event
    45	that the direction is nonzero at `i`, the leading index is `i` and the
    46	question is the canonical direct question of the direct sample `(p, i, v)`.
    47	Otherwise the restricted direction is also the restriction at the next index,
    48	so the mature quantity recurses with the factor `q⁻¹`, the probability that
    49	the sampled coordinate vanishes.  At the last index the zero direction has the
    50	last coordinate as its leading index by convention, and no recursion occurs. -/
    51	
    52	section DirectionCoordinates
    53	
    54	variable (D : DirectLdParams)
    55	
    56	/-- Restricting at an index where the direction vanishes is restricting at the
    57	next index. -/
    58	private theorem directPrefixProjection_succ_of_zero
    59	    (i i' : Fin D.m) (hi : i'.val = i.val + 1)
    60	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (hv : v i = 0) :
    61	    directPrefixProjection i v = directPrefixProjection i' v := by
    62	  funext j
    63	  unfold directPrefixProjection
    64	  by_cases hj : j.val < i.val
    65	  · rw [if_pos hj, if_pos (by omega)]
    66	  · by_cases hj' : j.val < i'.val
    67	    · rw [if_neg hj, if_pos hj']
    68	      have hji : j = i := Fin.ext (by omega)
    69	      rw [hji, hv]
    70	    · rw [if_neg hj, if_neg hj']
    71	
    72	/-- Restriction beyond a coordinate ignores translation along that
    73	coordinate. -/
    74	private theorem directPrefixProjection_add_single
    75	    (i i' : Fin D.m) (hi : i.val < i'.val)
    76	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (c : DirectScalarQ D) :
    77	    directPrefixProjection i' (v + c • Pi.single i (1 : DirectScalarQ D)) =
    78	      directPrefixProjection i' v := by
    79	  funext j
    80	  unfold directPrefixProjection
    81	  by_cases hj : j.val < i'.val
    82	  · rw [if_pos hj, if_pos hj]
    83	  · rw [if_neg hj, if_neg hj]
    84	    have hji : j ≠ i := by
    85	      intro h
    86	      apply hj
    87	      rw [h]
    88	      exact hi
    89	    simp [Pi.single_eq_of_ne hji]
    90	
    91	/-- At the last coordinate the restricted direction has that coordinate as
    92	its leading index: either the direction is nonzero there, or the restricted
    93	direction is zero and the leading index of the zero direction is the last
    94	coordinate by convention. -/
    95	private theorem directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection_last
    96	    (i : Fin D.m) (hi : i.val + 1 = D.m) (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
    97	    directDiagonalIndexOf D (directPrefixProjection i v) = i := by
    98	  by_cases hv : v i = 0
    99	  · have hzero : directPrefixProjection i v = 0 := by
   100	      funext j
   101	      unfold directPrefixProjection
   102	      by_cases hj : j.val < i.val
   103	      · rw [if_pos hj]
   104	        rfl
   105	      · rw [if_neg hj]
   106	        have hji : j = i := Fin.ext (by have := j.isLt; omega)
   107	        rw [hji, hv]
   108	        rfl
   109	    rw [hzero]
   110	    have hsupp : ¬ (directionSupport D (0 : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)).Nonempty := by
   111	      rintro ⟨j, hj⟩
   112	      exact (mem_directionSupport D 0 j).mp hj rfl
   113	    unfold directDiagonalIndexOf
   114	    rw [dif_neg hsupp]
   115	    apply Fin.ext
   116	    rw [Fin.val_rev]
   117	    simp only [DirectLdParams.firstIndex]
   118	    omega
   119	  · exact directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection D i v hv

   121	/-- Restricting to the vanishing of a coordinate below the restriction index
   122	scales the uniform average by the inverse field size: translation along that
   123	coordinate permutes the directions and preserves the restriction. -/
   124	private theorem avgOver_uniform_coord_zero (i i' : Fin D.m) (hi : i.val < i'.val)
   125	    (G : (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → ℝ) :
   126	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   127	        (fun v => if v i = 0 then G (directPrefixProjection i' v) else 0) =
   128	      (Fintype.card (DirectScalarQ D) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
   129	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   130	          (fun v => G (directPrefixProjection i' v)) := by
   131	  classical
   132	  have hshift : ∀ c : DirectScalarQ D,
   133	      (∑ v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D,
   134	        if v i = c then G (directPrefixProjection i' v) else 0) =
   135	      ∑ v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D,
   136	        if v i = 0 then G (directPrefixProjection i' v) else 0 := by
   137	    intro c
   138	    refine Fintype.sum_equiv
   139	      (Equiv.addRight ((-c) • Pi.single i (1 : DirectScalarQ D))) _ _ ?_
   140	    intro v
   141	    rw [Equiv.coe_addRight, directPrefixProjection_add_single D i i' hi]
   142	    simp only [Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, Pi.single_eq_same, smul_eq_mul, mul_one,
   143	      add_neg_eq_zero]
   144	  have hsum : (∑ v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D, G (directPrefixProjection i' v)) =
   145	      (Fintype.card (DirectScalarQ D) : ℝ) *
   146	        ∑ v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D,
   147	          if v i = 0 then G (directPrefixProjection i' v) else 0 := by
   148	    calc
   149	      (∑ v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D, G (directPrefixProjection i' v)) =
   150	          ∑ v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D, ∑ c : DirectScalarQ D,
   151	            if v i = c then G (directPrefixProjection i' v) else 0 := by
   152	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun v _ => ?_
   153	        rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq]
   154	        simp
   155	      _ = ∑ c : DirectScalarQ D, ∑ v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D,
   156	            if v i = c then G (directPrefixProjection i' v) else 0 :=
   157	        Finset.sum_comm
   158	      _ = ∑ c : DirectScalarQ D, ∑ v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D,
   159	            if v i = 0 then G (directPrefixProjection i' v) else 0 :=
   160	        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => hshift c
   161	      _ = _ := by
   162	        rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]
   163	  have hq : (Fintype.card (DirectScalarQ D) : ℝ) ≠ 0 :=
   164	    Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
   165	  rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum, avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum, hsum,
   166	    mul_left_comm, ← mul_assoc ((Fintype.card (DirectScalarQ D) : ℝ)⁻¹)
   167	      (Fintype.card (DirectScalarQ D) : ℝ), inv_mul_cancel₀ hq, one_mul]

   169	/-- Split a direct direction into the mature free coordinates of the
   170	`j`-restricted diagonal test, read in reversed coordinate order, and the
   171	coordinates below the reversed index. -/
   172	private def restrictedDirectionEquiv (j : Fin D.m) :
   173	    (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ≃
   174	      (Fin (j.val + 1) → Fq D.toLDTParameters) ×
   175	        (Fin (Fin.rev j).val → DirectScalarQ D) where
   176	  toFun v :=
   177	    (fun c => directScalarEquiv D (v ⟨D.m - 1 - c.val, by have := D.hm; omega⟩),
   178	      fun c => v ⟨c.val, by
   179	        have h1 := c.isLt
   180	        have h2 := Fin.val_rev j
   181	        omega⟩)
   182	  invFun x := fun c =>
   183	    if h : c.val < (Fin.rev j).val then x.2 ⟨c.val, h⟩
   184	    else (directScalarEquiv D).symm
   185	      (x.1 ⟨D.m - 1 - c.val, by
   186	        have h1 := c.isLt
   187	        have h2 := j.isLt
   188	        have h3 := Fin.val_rev j
   189	        omega⟩)
   190	  left_inv v := by
   191	    funext c
   192	    by_cases h : c.val < (Fin.rev j).val
   193	    · simp only [dif_pos h, Fin.eta]
   194	    · simp only [dif_neg h, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
   195	      refine congrArg v (Fin.ext ?_)
   196	      change D.m - 1 - (D.m - 1 - c.val) = c.val
   197	      have h1 := c.isLt
   198	      have h2 := D.hm
   199	      omega
   200	  right_inv x := by
   201	    refine Prod.ext ?_ ?_
   202	    · funext c
   203	      have h1 := c.isLt
   204	      have h2 := j.isLt
   205	      have h3 := Fin.val_rev j
   206	      have hc : ¬ (D.m - 1 - c.val < (Fin.rev j).val) := by omega
   207	      simp only [dif_neg hc, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
   208	      refine congrArg x.1 (Fin.ext ?_)
   209	      change D.m - 1 - (D.m - 1 - c.val) = c.val
   210	      omega
   211	    · funext c
   212	      simp only [dif_pos c.isLt, Fin.eta]

   214	/-- The decoded `j`-restricted mature direction of the free coordinates is the
   215	restriction of the direction at the reversed index. -/
   216	private theorem ldtPointToDirect_extend_restrictedDirectionEquiv (j : Fin D.m)
   217	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   218	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   219	    ldtPointToDirect D
   220	        (extendRestrictedDirection j (restrictedDirectionEquiv D j v).1) =
   221	      directPrefixProjection (Fin.rev j) v := by

   231	    have hle : (Fin.rev c).val ≤ j.val := by omega

   271	/-- Geometric-series bookkeeping for the one-coordinate recursion.  If every
   272	term is at most its rejection term plus `q⁻¹` times the term at the next
   273	index, and the term at the last index is at most its rejection term, then the
   274	sum is at most twice the sum of the rejection terms once `q ≥ 2`. -/
   275	private theorem sum_le_two_mul_sum_of_recursion {m : ℕ} (t r : Fin m → ℝ) (q : ℝ)
   276	    (hq : 2 ≤ q) (ht : ∀ i, 0 ≤ t i)
   277	    (hstep : ∀ i i' : Fin m, i'.val = i.val + 1 → t i ≤ r i + q⁻¹ * t i')
   278	    (hlast : ∀ i : Fin m, i.val + 1 = m → t i ≤ r i) :
   279	    ∑ i, t i ≤ 2 * ∑ i, r i := by
   280	  classical
   281	  have hq0 : (0 : ℝ) < q := by linarith
   282	  have hqinv : q⁻¹ ≤ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ := inv_anti₀ (by norm_num) hq
   283	  have hqinv0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ q⁻¹ := inv_nonneg.mpr hq0.le
   284	  let succSum : Fin m → ℝ := fun i =>
   285	    ∑ i' : Fin m, if i'.val = i.val + 1 then t i' else 0
   286	  have hbound : ∀ i, t i ≤ r i + q⁻¹ * succSum i := by
   287	    intro i
   288	    by_cases h : i.val + 1 < m
   289	    · have hsucc : succSum i = t ⟨i.val + 1, h⟩ := by
   290	        simp only [succSum]
   291	        rw [Finset.sum_eq_single ⟨i.val + 1, h⟩]
   292	        · simp
   293	        · intro b _ hb
   294	          rw [if_neg]
   295	          intro hb'
   296	          exact hb (Fin.ext hb')
   297	        · intro habs
   298	          exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ _) habs
   299	      rw [hsucc]
   300	      exact hstep i ⟨i.val + 1, h⟩ rfl
   301	    · have hlast' : i.val + 1 = m := by
   302	        have := i.isLt
   303	        omega
   304	      have hsucc : succSum i = 0 := by
   305	        simp only [succSum]
   306	        refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun i' _ => ?_
   307	        rw [if_neg]
   308	        intro h'
   309	        have := i'.isLt
   310	        omega
   311	      rw [hsucc, mul_zero, add_zero]
   312	      exact hlast i hlast'
   313	  have hsuccSum : ∑ i, succSum i ≤ ∑ i, t i := by
   314	    simp only [succSum]
   315	    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   316	    refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun i' _ => ?_
   317	    rw [← Finset.sum_filter, Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
   318	    have hcard :
   319	        ((Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin m => i'.val = i.val + 1).card : ℝ) ≤ 1 := by
   320	      have h1 : (Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin m => i'.val = i.val + 1).card ≤ 1 := by
   321	        rw [Finset.card_le_one]
   322	        intro a ha b hb
   323	        simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at ha hb
   324	        exact Fin.ext (by omega)
   325	      exact_mod_cast h1
   326	    calc ((Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin m => i'.val = i.val + 1).card : ℝ) * t i'
   327	        ≤ 1 * t i' := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hcard (ht i')
   328	      _ = t i' := one_mul _
   329	  have htotal : ∑ i, t i ≤ ∑ i, r i + q⁻¹ * ∑ i, t i := by
   330	    calc ∑ i, t i ≤ ∑ i, (r i + q⁻¹ * succSum i) := Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => hbound i
   331	      _ = ∑ i, r i + q⁻¹ * ∑ i, succSum i := by
   332	        rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.mul_sum]
   333	      _ ≤ ∑ i, r i + q⁻¹ * ∑ i, t i := by
   334	        linarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsuccSum hqinv0]
   335	  have hT : 0 ≤ ∑ i, t i := Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => ht i
   336	  have hhalf : q⁻¹ * ∑ i, t i ≤ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, t i :=
   337	    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hqinv hT
   338	  linarith

   342	variable (D : DirectLdParams)
   343	
   344	/-- One step of the recursion at a fixed point.  On the generic event the
   345	leading index is the sampled index and the mature defect is bounded by the
   346	direct rejection there; on the vanishing event the restriction agrees with the
   347	restriction at the next index. -/
   348	private theorem diagonal_recursion_step
   349	    (dd : (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → ℝ)
   350	    (rj : Fin D.m → (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → ℝ)
   351	    (hrj : ∀ i v, 0 ≤ rj i v)
   352	    (hdd : ∀ v, dd v ≤ rj (directDiagonalIndexOf D v) v)
   353	    (i i' : Fin D.m) (hi : i'.val = i.val + 1) :
   354	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   355	        (fun v => dd (directPrefixProjection i v)) ≤
   356	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   357	          (fun v => rj i (directPrefixProjection i v)) +
   358	        (Fintype.card (DirectScalarQ D) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
   359	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   360	            (fun v => dd (directPrefixProjection i' v)) := by
   361	  classical
   362	  have hsplit : ∀ v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D,
   363	      dd (directPrefixProjection i v) =
   364	        (if v i = 0 then 0 else dd (directPrefixProjection i v)) +
   365	          (if v i = 0 then dd (directPrefixProjection i' v) else 0) := by
   366	    intro v
   367	    by_cases hv : v i = 0
   368	    · rw [if_pos hv, if_pos hv, zero_add,
   369	        directPrefixProjection_succ_of_zero D i i' hi v hv]
   370	    · rw [if_neg hv, if_neg hv, add_zero]
   371	  rw [avgOver_congr _ _ _ hsplit, avgOver_add,
   372	    avgOver_uniform_coord_zero D i i' (by omega) dd]
   373	  refine add_le_add ?_ le_rfl
   374	  refine avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun v => ?_
   375	  by_cases hv : v i = 0
   376	  · rw [if_pos hv]
   377	    exact hrj i _
   378	  · rw [if_neg hv]
   379	    calc dd (directPrefixProjection i v) ≤
   380	        rj (directDiagonalIndexOf D (directPrefixProjection i v))
   381	          (directPrefixProjection i v) := hdd _
   382	      _ = rj i (directPrefixProjection i v) := by
   383	        rw [directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection D i v hv]
   384	
   385	/-- At the last index the mature defect is bounded by the direct rejection
   386	without recursion. -/
   387	private theorem diagonal_recursion_last
   388	    (dd : (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → ℝ)
   389	    (rj : Fin D.m → (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → ℝ)
   390	    (hdd : ∀ v, dd v ≤ rj (directDiagonalIndexOf D v) v)
   391	    (i : Fin D.m) (hi : i.val + 1 = D.m) :
   392	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   393	        (fun v => dd (directPrefixProjection i v)) ≤
   394	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   395	        (fun v => rj i (directPrefixProjection i v)) := by
   396	  refine avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun v => ?_
   397	  calc dd (directPrefixProjection i v) ≤
   398	      rj (directDiagonalIndexOf D (directPrefixProjection i v))
   399	        (directPrefixProjection i v) := hdd _
   400	    _ = rj i (directPrefixProjection i v) := by
   401	      rw [directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection_last D i hi v]
   402	
   403	/-- Summed over the restriction index, the mature diagonal quantities at a
   404	fixed point are at most twice the direct rejections. -/
   405	private theorem diagonal_sum_le
   406	    (dd : (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → ℝ)
   407	    (rj : Fin D.m → (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → ℝ)
   408	    (hdd0 : ∀ v, 0 ≤ dd v) (hrj : ∀ i v, 0 ≤ rj i v)
   409	    (hdd : ∀ v, dd v ≤ rj (directDiagonalIndexOf D v) v) :
   410	    ∑ i : Fin D.m, avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   411	        (fun v => dd (directPrefixProjection i v)) ≤
   412	      2 * ∑ i : Fin D.m, avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   413	        (fun v => rj i (directPrefixProjection i v)) := by
   414	  have hcard : 2 ≤ Fintype.card (DirectScalarQ D) := Fintype.one_lt_card
   415	  refine sum_le_two_mul_sum_of_recursion _ _ (Fintype.card (DirectScalarQ D) : ℝ)
   416	    (by exact_mod_cast hcard) ?_ ?_ ?_
   417	  · intro i
   418	    exact avgOver_nonneg _ _ fun v => hdd0 _
   419	  · intro i i' hi
   420	    exact diagonal_recursion_step D dd rj hrj hdd i i' hi
   421	  · intro i hi
   422	    exact diagonal_recursion_last D dd rj hdd i hi
   423	
   424	end DiagonalRecursion

   495	            (S.A (directDiagonalQuestionOf D (matureDiagonalLineOf D ⟨p, D.firstIndex, v⟩)))

   619	/-- Summing a decoded diagonal quantity over the reversed index is summing it
   620	over the direct index, and the point average may be taken outside. -/
   621	private theorem sum_rev_avgOver_eq
   622	    (F : (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → Fin D.m → (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → ℝ) :
   623	    ∑ j : Fin D.m, avgOver (uniformDistribution
   624	        ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)))
   625	        (fun pv => F pv.1 (Fin.rev j) (directPrefixProjection (Fin.rev j) pv.2)) =
   626	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) fun p =>
   627	        ∑ i : Fin D.m, avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   628	          (fun v => F p i (directPrefixProjection i v)) := by
   629	  rw [avgOver_sum]
   630	  have hrev := Equiv.sum_comp Fin.revPerm (fun i =>
   631	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) fun p =>
   632	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   633	        (fun v => F p i (directPrefixProjection i v)))
   634	  simp only [Fin.revPerm_apply] at hrev
   635	  rw [← hrev]
   636	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
   637	  exact avgOver_uniform_prod (fun p v => F p (Fin.rev j) (directPrefixProjection (Fin.rev j) v))

   639	/-- The direct index average of a diagonal quantity, with the point average
   640	taken outside. -/
   641	private theorem avgOver_index_eq
   642	    (F : (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → Fin D.m → (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → ℝ) :
   643	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m)) (fun i =>
   644	        avgOver (uniformDistribution
   645	          ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)))
   646	          (fun pv => F pv.1 i (directPrefixProjection i pv.2))) =
   647	      (D.m : ℝ)⁻¹ * avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) fun p =>
   648	        ∑ i : Fin D.m, avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   649	          (fun v => F p i (directPrefixProjection i v)) := by
   650	  rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum, Fintype.card_fin, avgOver_sum]
   651	  congr 1
   652	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
   653	  exact avgOver_uniform_prod (fun p v => F p i (directPrefixProjection i v))

   655	/-- The diagonal-line failure with the line on the left is at most twice the
   656	diagonal-line/point branch rejection of the direct game. -/
   657	theorem directCoordinate_diagonal_line_point_le :
   658	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   659	    (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).diagonalLineLeftPointRightFailureProbability ≤
   660	      2 * directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S (.dline, .point) := by
   661	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   662	  unfold ProjStrat.diagonalLineLeftPointRightFailureProbability
   663	  rw [diagonal_line_point_branch_eq, avgOver_index_eq,
   664	    Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => diagonal_line_point_term_eq D S hS r j),
   665	    sum_rev_avgOver_eq D (fun p _ v => diagonalLinePointDefect D S hS r p v), one_div]
   666	  have hmain :
   667	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) (fun p =>
   668	          ∑ i : Fin D.m, avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   669	            (fun v => diagonalLinePointDefect D S hS r p (directPrefixProjection i v))) ≤
   670	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) (fun p =>
   671	          2 * ∑ i : Fin D.m, avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   672	            (fun v => diagonalLinePointRejection D S p i (directPrefixProjection i v))) := by
   673	    refine avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun p => ?_
   674	    exact diagonal_sum_le D (fun v => diagonalLinePointDefect D S hS r p v)
   675	      (fun i v => diagonalLinePointRejection D S p i v)
   676	      (fun v => qBipartiteConsDefect_nonneg _ _ _)
   677	      (fun i v => directRejectedMass_nonneg D S _ _)
   678	      (fun v => diagonalLinePointDefect_le D S hS r p v)
   679	  rw [avgOver_const_mul] at hmain
   680	  have hm : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (D.m : ℝ)⁻¹ := by positivity
   681	  calc (D.m : ℝ)⁻¹ * _ ≤ (D.m : ℝ)⁻¹ * (2 * _) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hmain hm
   682	    _ = _ := by ring
   683	
   684	/-- The diagonal-line failure with the point on the left is at most twice the
   685	point/diagonal-line branch rejection of the direct game. -/
   686	theorem directCoordinate_diagonal_point_line_le :
   687	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   688	    (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).diagonalPointLeftLineRightFailureProbability ≤
   689	      2 * directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S (.point, .dline) := by
   690	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   691	  unfold ProjStrat.diagonalPointLeftLineRightFailureProbability
   692	  rw [diagonal_point_line_branch_eq, avgOver_index_eq,
   693	    Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => diagonal_point_line_term_eq D S hS r j),
   694	    sum_rev_avgOver_eq D (fun p _ v => diagonalPointLineDefect D S hS r p v), one_div]
   695	  have hmain :
   696	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) (fun p =>
   697	          ∑ i : Fin D.m, avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   698	            (fun v => diagonalPointLineDefect D S hS r p (directPrefixProjection i v))) ≤
   699	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) (fun p =>
   700	          2 * ∑ i : Fin D.m, avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   701	            (fun v => diagonalPointLineRejection D S p i (directPrefixProjection i v))) := by
   702	    refine avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun p => ?_
   703	    exact diagonal_sum_le D (fun v => diagonalPointLineDefect D S hS r p v)
   704	      (fun i v => diagonalPointLineRejection D S p i v)
   705	      (fun v => qBipartiteConsDefect_nonneg _ _ _)
   706	      (fun i v => directRejectedMass_nonneg D S _ _)
   707	      (fun v => diagonalPointLineDefect_le D S hS r p v)
   708	  rw [avgOver_const_mul] at hmain
   709	  have hm : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (D.m : ℝ)⁻¹ := by positivity
   710	  calc (D.m : ℝ)⁻¹ * _ ≤ (D.m : ℝ)⁻¹ * (2 * _) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hmain hm
   711	    _ = _ := by ring

     3	/-!
     4	# Value of the seed-fiber dilation
     5	
     6	The correlated seed-fiber dilation `ldStrategyToDirect` reads a strategy for
     7	the seed-indexed low-degree game as a strategy for the directly indexed game.
     8	This module shows that the dilation preserves the value exactly.
     9	
    10	The direct game asks the canonical questions of a common direct sample.  In
    11	each residue block the dilated strategy asks the original strategy the seeded
    12	canonical questions of that sample; since canonicalizing a canonical sample
    13	changes nothing, these are the seed-indexed questions of the common sample
    14	carrying that residue.  The Born weight of the dilation is the uniform average
    15	of the original Born weights over the residue, the predicates agree after
    16	parsing, and the seed-indexed sample is a direct sample together with a
    17	uniform residue, so the two averages coincide branch by branch, including the

## 5. Review Checklist

Every PR touching Lean code should be reviewed against these criteria:

1. **Proof correctness** -- No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.
   Run `rg -n "sorry|axiom" <file>` to verify.

2. **Mathlib style** -- Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and
   `MATHLIB_doc` references. See the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review`
   reference for the full Mathlib review guide.

3. **Paper terminology** -- Public Lean names, module docstrings, declaration
   docstrings, and documentation-visible comments should use terminology from
   the paper and blueprint, not implementation history. See
   [mathematical_language.md](mathematical_language.md) for the project-local
   language rule for Lean documentation and public names. Reviewers should flag
   names that encode historical formalization status rather than mathematical
   content. When an old public identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR,
   record the required migration in the issue, PR description, or an audit file
   under [audits/](../audits/).
   New and substantively updated audit files should follow the term norm and
   format in
   [audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md](../audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md).
   Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   public name.
   Review-fix PRs must read the relevant audit files under [audits/](../audits/)
   before changing names or prose. If an audit marks a naming migration or
   historical-formalization term as in scope for the fix, addressing it or
   explicitly updating the audit trail is a merge blocker.

4. **Linter hygiene** -- Linter-warning cleanup must fix warnings, not mask
   them with broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks. See
   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md#linter-warnings) for the project rule and the narrow
   exception policy.

5. **Type safety** -- No universe mismatches, coercion problems, or unresolved
   metavariables.

6. **Performance** -- Avoid expensive tactics on large types (e.g., `decide` on
   `Fin 1000`). Watch for timeout-prone proof terms.

7. **Modularity** -- Are new lemmas general enough to be reused? Could any be
   upstreamed to Mathlib?

8. **Documentation** -- Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.
   Module files should have a header comment with `## References` citing the
   relevant arXiv paper(s).

9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** -- If the PR formalizes a statement
   from the blueprint, add `\lean{LeanDeclName}` and `\leanok` tags to the
   corresponding `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file. If the PR adds a public
   auxiliary lemma that is not a named statement in the original paper, record
   that explicitly: the Lean docstring should call it a formalization-only
   auxiliary lemma and the blueprint should either omit it as private/internal
   infrastructure or include it as a clearly subordinate support node connected
   by `\uses{...}`. See
   [blueprint_style_guide.md](blueprint_style_guide.md#recording-formalization-only-lemmas).
   PR descriptions and follow-up issues should cite the corresponding paper or
   blueprint path, line, label, and a short quotation or precise paraphrase.
   Reviewers should also check for early drift from the source: new hypotheses,
   weakened conclusions, changed quantifier order, altered error parameters,
   or renamed obligation structures that turn a paper theorem into a conditional
   theorem.  If such drift appears, request a statement integrity audit before
   reviewing the proof.  A bridge or residual hypothesis should be treated as
   proof debt to remove, not as evidence that the paper statement has been
   formalized.

10. **Scaffolding integrity** -- If the PR introduces or modifies scaffolded
   definitions (types, theorem statements with `sorry` proofs), verify that
   the types and API surface align with Mathlib. Scaffolding that uses custom
   types incompatible with Mathlib blocks future proof work. See
   the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and
   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md) for details.

11. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** -- Review against
   [anti_patterns.md](anti_patterns.md), which catalogues subtler failure
   modes that pass the proof-integrity blocker checks but still fail
   to prove the claimed mathematics: conclusion-shaped hypotheses (A1),
   `:= rfl` definitional sleight-of-hand (A2), zero-fallback branches
   hiding preconditions (A3), trivial default witnesses (A4),
   Mathlib-bypass castles (A5), and external `*Statement` smuggles (A6).
   Use the reviewer checklist at the end of that file.

12. **Proof frontier integrity** -- If the PR introduces or threads structure
   fields such as `*Input`, `*Residual`, `*BridgeInputs`, `*Witness`,
   `*Statement`, `*Conclusion`, or `*Package`, review it against
   [proof_frontier_review.md](proof_frontier_review.md). A PR that only
   repackages an assumption should not be described as proving the corresponding
   paper step; it must name the missing obligation discharger or link the native
   sub-issue that tracks it.  For source-labelled theorems, the preferred repair
   is to extract any usable proof content into source-faithful lemmas and
   restore the paper-aligned statement, even if the remaining proof is a tracked
   `sorry` during the cleanup.  For source-labelled proof gaps, also use the
   protocol in
   [paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex).

### Semantic scaffold checklist (required for core math objects)

For semantic objects such as measurements, submeasurements, distributions,
averaged operators, and packaged theorem outputs, reviewers should additionally
verify:

1. **Impossible states check** -- Does the structure exclude states that are
   impossible under the paper definition?
2. **Derived-field check** -- If a field is mathematically derived
   (e.g. `total = ∑ a, outcome a`), is it either derived on demand or stored
   together with an equality proof (e.g. `sum_eq_total`)?
3. **Invariant bundling check** -- Are core invariants (positivity,
   boundedness/normalization, completeness where applicable) encoded directly
   in the structure or constructor, rather than deferred to downstream lemmas?
4. **Stress-test check** -- Is at least one nontrivial theorem in scope of the
   PR provable/stated against the scaffold without adding ad hoc assumptions?

If any answer is "no", treat the scaffold as unsafe and request a follow-up
before broad theorem layering continues.

## 6. Lean Code Style

This project follows Mathlib conventions with project-specific additions.

### Reference guides

Shared references (the `lean-conventions` skill of
texra-ai/texra-lean-skills, auto-installed via `.claude/settings.json`):

- **Documentation style**: the `MATHLIB_doc` reference -- module headers,
  docstrings, LaTeX in comments, sectioning comments.
- **Naming conventions**: the `MATHLIB_naming` reference -- capitalization
  rules, symbol-to-name dictionary, variable conventions.
- **Review guide**: the `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference -- detailed examples of
  style, documentation, location, and improvement considerations.

MIPStarRE-local references:

- **Mathematical language**: [mathematical_language.md](mathematical_language.md)
  -- project-local terminology rules for Lean names and documentation.
- **Proof integrity**: the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference plus
  the addenda in [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md) -- blocker
  and warning patterns for proof correctness.
- **Blueprint style**: [blueprint_style_guide.md](blueprint_style_guide.md) --
  notation and section conventions for the active blueprint.

### Project-specific conventions

**Module header**: Every `.lean` file should start with a module docstring that
includes:

```lean
/-!
# Title

Summary of what this file contains.

## Main definitions / statements

- `FooBar` : description
- `fooBar_baz` : description

## References

- [arXiv:XXXX.XXXXX](https://arxiv.org/abs/XXXX.XXXXX) -- Author, *Title*
-/
```

**Docstrings**: Required on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant
`theorem`. Encouraged on supporting lemmas. Use Markdown; refer to Lean
identifiers in backticks.

**Sectioning comments**: Use `/-! ### Section Title -/` to organize long files
into logical sections.

**Variable naming**: Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` reference. For
this project specifically:
- `q` for alphabet size / finite field order
- `n`, `m` for dimension parameters
- `σ` for strategies
- `P` for projective measurements
- `G` for graphs (hypercube expansion)

## 7. CI & Automation

The following workflows run automatically:

| Workflow | Trigger | What it does |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| **Lean CI** (`pr-ci.yml` (`build` job)) | Push to `main`, PRs touching `.lean`/`lakefile.toml`/`lean-toolchain` | Runs `lake build` with Mathlib cache |
| **PR Review** (`pr-review.yml`, `code-review` jobs) | After a successful PR CI run | Automated review for proof integrity, Mathlib style, type safety, performance, modularity, mathematical exposition, and documentation |
| **Issue Automation** (`issue-automation.yml`) | Issue opened/labeled/closed/reopened; PR opened/merged | Classifies new issues, posts Mathlib scouting reports, keeps tracking issues current via a deterministic script (progress comments, sub-issue counts, and a ready-to-close notice when every sub-issue is resolved), and scans merged PRs for genuine deferred mathematical obligations, filing `follow-up` issues |
| **Blueprint Lint** (`pr-ci.yml` (`blueprint-render` job)) | PRs touching blueprint files | Builds `leanblueprint pdf` / `web` to catch broken labels, undefined macros, and plasTeX errors, then runs the blueprint ↔ Lean sync checks. The LaTeX convention scan and the `scripts/tests` helper unit tests both run locally in the pre-commit hook. |
| **Blueprint Sync & Prose Review** (`pr-review.yml`, `prose-review` job) | After a successful PR CI run | Reviews blueprint synchronization, source-faithfulness, and mathematical prose for formalization changes. |
| **README Freshness Audit** (`housekeeping.yml`, `readme-freshness` job) | Weekly + manual dispatch | Report-only audit for README local paths, LDT submodule count, and hard-coded Lean/Mathlib versions |
| **PR Mathematical Description** (`pr-cleanup.yml`) | PR opened from `claude/*` or `codex/*` branches | Normalizes title to `type(scope): desc`, rewrites the PR body as a self-contained mathematical note, preserves source citations from the linked issue, copies labels, adds `Addresses #N`, and comments on the issue |
| **Mathlib Scout** (`issue-automation.yml`, `scout` job) | Formalization issue opened/labeled | Scouts Mathlib for relevant lemmas and posts a scouting report |

### What CI checks before merge

- `lake build MIPStarRE` must succeed (no type errors, no broken imports).
- No new `sorry` without explicit justification.
- Blueprint labels must resolve (no broken `\ref` or `\label`).
- Claude Code Review should not flag critical issues (proof correctness,
  type safety).

     3	/-!
     4	# Question and answer transport for the directly indexed low-degree game
     5	
     6	This module reads mature low individual degree questions as canonical direct
     7	questions and rebases direct answers to the mature line parametrization.
     8	
     9	Points and lines are decoded with the coordinate order reversed
    10	(`directPointEquiv`), so that the suffix-zero direction restriction of the
    11	mature diagonal test becomes the prefix-zero restriction of the direct game.
    12	A mature diagonal line reveals no coordinate index, whereas a direct diagonal
    13	question carries one.  The transported question uses the *leading index* of
    14	the decoded direction, the least coordinate at which the direction is
    15	nonzero.  Under the direct sampler, this is the index attached to the sampled
    16	direction exactly when the direction is nonzero at the sampled index
    17	(`directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection`), an event of conditional
    18	probability `1 - 1/q`; on the mature side, the leading index of a decoded
    19	`j`-restricted direction is `Fin.rev j` exactly when its pivot coordinate is
    20	nonzero (`directDiagonalIndexOf_extendRestrictedDirection`).  Diagonal answers
    21	on zero-direction lines are read as the constant polynomial carrying their
    22	value at the base point, following `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
    23	
    24	## References
    25	
    26	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:230-272`
    27	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:49-65`
    28	- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:120-121`
    29	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    30	-/

    32	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    33	
    34	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    35	
    36	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    37	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    38	
    39	noncomputable section
    40	
    41	/-! ## Canonical line rebasing for the mature LDT interface -/
    42	
    43	/-- A chosen affine parameter expressing a point relative to its canonical
    44	line representative. -/
    45	noncomputable def directLineRepParameter
    46	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) : K :=
    47	  Classical.choose (mem_linePoints_lineRepMap v u)
    48	
    49	/-- The chosen canonical rebase parameter reconstructs the original point. -/
    50	theorem directLineRepParameter_spec
    51	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) :
    52	    u = lineRepMap v u + directLineRepParameter v u • v :=
    53	  Classical.choose_spec (mem_linePoints_lineRepMap v u)
    54	
    55	/-- Canonical line representatives are unchanged by translation along their
    56	direction. -/
    57	theorem lineRepMap_add_smul
    58	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    59	    (v u : Fin m → K) (t : K) :
    60	    lineRepMap v (u + t • v) = lineRepMap v u := by
    61	  let W : Submodule K (Fin m → K) := Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))
    62	  have hv : v ∈ W := Submodule.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton v)
    63	  have hzero : lineRepMap v v = 0 := by
    64	    simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, W, LinearMap.comp_apply,
    65	      Submodule.projectionOnto_apply_of_mem_right
    66	        (isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement W).symm hv]
    67	  simp [map_add, map_smul, hzero]
    68	
    69	/-- For a nonzero direction, the canonical rebase parameter is unique. -/
    70	theorem directLineRepParameter_eq_of_nonzero
    71	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    72	    {v u : Fin m → K} (hv : v ≠ 0) {t : K}
    73	    (ht : u = lineRepMap v u + t • v) :
    74	    directLineRepParameter v u = t := by
    75	  have hfun : directLineRepParameter v u • v = t • v := by
    76	    apply add_left_cancel (a := lineRepMap v u)
    77	    exact (directLineRepParameter_spec v u).symm.trans ht
    78	  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, v i ≠ 0 := by
    79	    by_contra h
    80	    apply hv
    81	    funext i
    82	    simpa using not_exists.mp h i
    83	  have hcoord := congrFun hfun i
    84	  simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] at hcoord
    85	  exact mul_right_cancel₀ hi hcoord
    86	
    87	/-- Translating a point on a nonzero line adds the translation to its
    88	canonical rebase parameter. -/
    89	theorem directLineRepParameter_add_smul
    90	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    91	    {v u : Fin m → K} (hv : v ≠ 0) (t : K) :
    92	    directLineRepParameter v (u + t • v) =
    93	      directLineRepParameter v u + t := by
    94	  apply directLineRepParameter_eq_of_nonzero hv
    95	  rw [lineRepMap_add_smul]
    96	  calc
    97	    u + t • v =
    98	        (lineRepMap v u + directLineRepParameter v u • v) + t • v := by
    99	      rw [← directLineRepParameter_spec v u]
   100	    _ = lineRepMap v u + (directLineRepParameter v u + t) • v := by

   102	
   103	/-! ## The leading index of a direction -/
   104	
   105	/-- The coordinates at which a direct direction vector is nonzero. -/
   106	def directionSupport (D : DirectLdParams) (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   107	    Finset (Fin D.m) :=
   108	  open Classical in
   109	  Finset.univ.filter fun j => v j ≠ 0
   110	
   111	theorem mem_directionSupport (D : DirectLdParams)
   112	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (j : Fin D.m) :
   113	    j ∈ directionSupport D v ↔ v j ≠ 0 := by
   114	  simp [directionSupport]
   115	
   116	/-- The leading index of a direction: the least coordinate at which it is
   117	nonzero, or the last coordinate for the zero direction.  Every coordinate
   118	before the leading index vanishes, so a direction is the prefix projection of
   119	itself at its leading index, and the pair (leading index, direction) is a
   120	canonical direct diagonal sample.  It is the direct index of the sample
   121	whenever the sampled direction is nonzero at the sampled index. -/
   122	noncomputable def directDiagonalIndexOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   123	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m :=
   124	  open Classical in
   125	  if h : (directionSupport D v).Nonempty then (directionSupport D v).min' h
   126	  else Fin.rev D.firstIndex
   127	
   128	/-- Coordinates before the leading index vanish. -/
   129	theorem directDiagonalIndexOf_prefix_zero (D : DirectLdParams)
   130	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   131	    ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < (directDiagonalIndexOf D v).val → v j = 0 := by
   132	  classical
   133	  intro j hj
   134	  by_contra hne
   135	  have hmem : j ∈ directionSupport D v := (mem_directionSupport D v j).mpr hne
   136	  have hnonempty : (directionSupport D v).Nonempty := ⟨j, hmem⟩
   137	  have hle : directDiagonalIndexOf D v ≤ j := by
   138	    unfold directDiagonalIndexOf
   139	    rw [dif_pos hnonempty]
   140	    exact Finset.min'_le _ _ hmem
   141	  exact absurd (Fin.lt_def.mpr hj) (not_lt.mpr hle)
   142	
   143	/-- A direction vanishing before `i` and nonzero at `i` has leading index
   144	`i`. -/
   145	theorem directDiagonalIndexOf_eq (D : DirectLdParams)
   146	    {v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D} {i : Fin D.m}
   147	    (hzero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < i.val → v j = 0) (hi : v i ≠ 0) :
   148	    directDiagonalIndexOf D v = i := by
   149	  classical
   150	  have hmem : i ∈ directionSupport D v := (mem_directionSupport D v i).mpr hi
   151	  have hnonempty : (directionSupport D v).Nonempty := ⟨i, hmem⟩
   152	  unfold directDiagonalIndexOf
   153	  rw [dif_pos hnonempty]
   154	  apply le_antisymm
   155	  · exact Finset.min'_le _ _ hmem
   156	  · apply Finset.le_min'
   157	    intro j hj
   158	    by_contra hlt
   159	    exact (mem_directionSupport D v j).mp hj
   160	      (hzero j (Fin.lt_def.mp (not_le.mp hlt)))
   161	
   162	/-- The leading index of a prefix-projected direction is the projection index
   163	whenever the direction is nonzero there.  This is the generic direct
   164	diagonal sample: the sampled index is recovered from the projected direction
   165	alone. -/
   166	theorem directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection (D : DirectLdParams)
   167	    (i : Fin D.m) (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (hi : v i ≠ 0) :
   168	    directDiagonalIndexOf D (directPrefixProjection i v) = i := by
   169	  apply directDiagonalIndexOf_eq
   170	  · intro j hj
   171	    simp [directPrefixProjection, hj]
   172	  · simpa [directPrefixProjection] using hi
   173	
   174	/-- Prefix projection at the leading index is the identity. -/
   175	theorem directPrefixProjection_directDiagonalIndexOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   176	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   177	    directPrefixProjection (directDiagonalIndexOf D v) v = v := by
   178	  funext j
   179	  unfold directPrefixProjection
   180	  split_ifs with hj
   181	  · exact (directDiagonalIndexOf_prefix_zero D v j hj).symm
   182	  · rfl
   183	
   184	/-! ## Decoding mature points and lines -/
   185	
   186	/-- Decode a mature LDT point into the fixed direct scalar field, reversing
   187	the coordinate order. -/
   188	abbrev ldtPointToDirect (D : DirectLdParams) :
   189	    Point D.toLDTParameters → Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   190	  (directPointEquiv D).symm
   191	
   192	/-- The direct canonical axis question represented by a mature axis line.
   193	The mature coordinate index is reversed together with the point
   194	coordinates. -/
   195	noncomputable def directAxisQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   196	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   197	  let u := ldtPointToDirect D line.base
   198	  let i : Fin D.m := Fin.rev line.direction
   199	  let v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D := coordinateDirection i
   200	  (.aline, ⟨lineRepMap v u, i, 0⟩)
   201	
   202	/-- The direct canonical diagonal question represented by a mature diagonal
   203	line.  The decoded direction is kept and the direct index is its leading
   204	index, so the question is the canonical direct question of the direct sample
   205	formed by the decoded base, the leading index, and the decoded direction
   206	(`directDiagonalQuestionOf_eq_directLdMap`). -/
   207	noncomputable def directDiagonalQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   208	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   209	  let u := ldtPointToDirect D line.base
   210	  let v := ldtPointToDirect D line.direction
   211	  (.dline, ⟨lineRepMap v u, directDiagonalIndexOf D v, v⟩)
   212	
   213	/-- The direct point question represented by a mature LDT point. -/
   214	noncomputable def directPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   215	    (u : Point D.toLDTParameters) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   216	  directLdPointQuestionOf D (ldtPointToDirect D u)
   217	
   218	/-- Every transported diagonal question is the canonical direct question of
   219	the direct sample carrying the leading index, hence lies in the support of
   220	the direct diagonal sampler. -/
   221	theorem directDiagonalQuestionOf_eq_directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams)
   222	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters) :
   223	    directDiagonalQuestionOf D line =
   224	      (.dline, directLdMap D .dline
   225	        ⟨ldtPointToDirect D line.base,
   226	          directDiagonalIndexOf D (ldtPointToDirect D line.direction),
   227	          ldtPointToDirect D line.direction⟩) := by
   228	  unfold directDiagonalQuestionOf directLdMap
   229	  simp only [directPrefixProjection_directDiagonalIndexOf]
   230	
   231	/-- The mature diagonal line represented by a direct sample: the encoded
   232	point and the encoded direction. -/
   233	def matureDiagonalLineOf (D : DirectLdParams) (sample : DirectLdSpace D) :
   234	    DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters :=
   235	  { base := directPointEquiv D sample.point
   236	    direction := directPointEquiv D sample.direction }
   237	
   238	/-- Round trip on generic direct samples: when the sampled direction is
   239	nonzero at the sampled index, the mature line of the canonical direct
   240	diagonal question transports back to that question, index included. -/
   241	theorem directDiagonalQuestionOf_matureDiagonalLineOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   242	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D)
   243	    (hgeneric : sample.direction sample.index ≠ 0) :
   244	    directDiagonalQuestionOf D
   245	        (matureDiagonalLineOf D (directLdMap D .dline sample)) =
   246	      (.dline, directLdMap D .dline sample) := by
   247	  cases sample with
   248	  | mk point index direction =>
   249	      unfold directDiagonalQuestionOf matureDiagonalLineOf directLdMap
   250	      simp only [ldtPointToDirect, Equiv.symm_apply_apply, lineRepMap_apply_self,
   251	        directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection D index direction hgeneric]
   252	
   253	/-- A mature `j`-restricted diagonal direction decodes to a direct direction
   254	vanishing before index `Fin.rev j`: the suffix restriction of the mature
   255	test is the prefix restriction of the direct game. -/
   256	theorem ldtPointToDirect_extendRestrictedDirection_prefix_zero
   257	    (D : DirectLdParams) (j : Fin D.m)
   258	    (free : Fin (j.val + 1) → Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   259	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   260	    ∀ c : Fin D.m, c.val < (Fin.rev j).val →
   261	      ldtPointToDirect D (extendRestrictedDirection j free) c = 0 := by
   262	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   263	  intro c hc
   264	  have hj := j.isLt
   265	  have hgt : ¬ (Fin.rev c).val ≤ j.val := by
   266	    rw [Fin.val_rev] at hc ⊢
   267	    omega
   268	  simp only [ldtPointToDirect, directPointEquiv_symm_apply,
   269	    extendRestrictedDirection, dif_neg hgt]
   270	  exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q)).symm_apply_apply 0
   271	
   272	/-- The leading index of a decoded `j`-restricted direction is `Fin.rev j`
   273	exactly on the generic event that its pivot coordinate `j` is nonzero. -/
   274	theorem directDiagonalIndexOf_extendRestrictedDirection
   275	    (D : DirectLdParams) (j : Fin D.m)
   276	    (free : Fin (j.val + 1) → Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   277	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   278	    free ⟨j.val, Nat.lt_succ_self _⟩ ≠ zeroCoord →
   279	      directDiagonalIndexOf D
   280	          (ldtPointToDirect D (extendRestrictedDirection j free)) =
   281	        Fin.rev j := by
   282	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   283	  intro hpivot
   284	  apply directDiagonalIndexOf_eq
   285	  · exact ldtPointToDirect_extendRestrictedDirection_prefix_zero D j free
   286	  · simp only [ldtPointToDirect, directPointEquiv_symm_apply, Fin.rev_rev,
   287	      extendRestrictedDirection, dif_pos (le_refl j.val)]
   288	    intro h
   289	    apply hpivot
   290	    have hcoded := congrArg (directScalarEquiv D) h
   291	    rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply] at hcoded
   292	    exact hcoded
   293	
   294	/-! ## Rebasing lines -/
   295	
   296	/-- Decoding an axis-line rebase is translation by the decoded scalar along
   297	the reversed direct coordinate direction. -/
   298	theorem ldtPointToDirect_axis_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   299	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters)
   300	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   301	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   302	    ldtPointToDirect D (line.rebaseAt t).base =
   303	      ldtPointToDirect D line.base +
   304	        (directScalarEquiv D).symm t •
   305	          coordinateDirection (Fin.rev line.direction) := by
   306	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   307	  funext i
   308	  simp only [ldtPointToDirect, directPointEquiv_symm_apply,
   309	    AxisParallelLine.rebaseAt, AxisParallelLine.pointAt, Pi.add_apply,
   310	    Pi.smul_apply]
   311	  by_cases hi : i = Fin.rev line.direction
   312	  · subst hi
   313	    simp only [coordinateDirection, Fin.rev_rev, if_pos, smul_eq_mul]
   314	    rw [Pi.single_eq_same, mul_one]
   315	    exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q)).symm_apply_apply _
   316	  · have hrev : Fin.rev i ≠ line.direction := by
   317	      intro h
   318	      apply hi
   319	      rw [← h, Fin.rev_rev]
   320	    simp [hi, hrev, coordinateDirection]
   321	
   322	/-- Decoding a diagonal-line rebase is translation by the decoded scalar
   323	along the decoded direct direction. -/
   324	theorem ldtPointToDirect_diagonal_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   325	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters)
   326	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   327	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   328	    ldtPointToDirect D (line.rebaseAt t).base =
   329	      ldtPointToDirect D line.base +
   330	        (directScalarEquiv D).symm t • ldtPointToDirect D line.direction := by
   331	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   332	  funext i
   333	  change decodeScalar
   334	      (addCoord (line.base (Fin.rev i))
   335	        (mulCoord t (line.direction (Fin.rev i)))) =
   336	    decodeScalar (line.base (Fin.rev i)) +
   337	      decodeScalar t * decodeScalar (line.direction (Fin.rev i))
   338	  simp [addCoord, mulCoord]
   339	
   340	/-- Canonical direct axis questions do not depend on the chosen base point of
   341	the mature line. -/
   342	theorem directAxisQuestionOf_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   343	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters)
   344	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   345	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   346	    directAxisQuestionOf D (line.rebaseAt t) = directAxisQuestionOf D line := by
   347	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   348	  simp only [directAxisQuestionOf, AxisParallelLine.rebaseAt_direction]
   349	  rw [ldtPointToDirect_axis_rebase, lineRepMap_add_smul]
   350	
   351	/-- Canonical direct diagonal questions do not depend on the chosen base point
   352	of the mature line; the leading index depends only on the direction. -/
   353	theorem directDiagonalQuestionOf_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   354	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters)
   355	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   356	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   357	    directDiagonalQuestionOf D (line.rebaseAt t) =
   358	      directDiagonalQuestionOf D line := by
   359	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   360	  simp only [directDiagonalQuestionOf, DiagonalLine.rebaseAt]

     6	# Geometry for the directly indexed low-degree game
     7	
     8	This module defines the parameters, line carrier, and line-point distributions
     9	for the directly indexed low-degree game.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The line-point distributions originate in
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`.
    15	The directly indexed repair is documented in
    16	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum

    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	/-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,
    30	this directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is
    31	sampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.
    32	
    33	This is the direct-index repair described in
    34	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second
    35	definition of the source verifier game. -/
    36	structure DirectLdParams where
    37	  q : ℕ
    38	  m : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  k : ℕ
    41	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    42	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    43	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    44	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    45	
    46	/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/
    47	noncomputable def DirectLdParams.model (D : DirectLdParams) : FixedFieldModel D.q :=
    48	  fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq
    49	
    50	/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/
    51	abbrev DirectScalarQ (D : DirectLdParams) := D.model.K
    52	
    53	/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are
    54	positive. -/
    55	def DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=
    56	  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm⟩
    57	
    58	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (Fin D.m) := ⟨D.firstIndex⟩
    59	
    60	/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its
    61	field, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its
    62	dimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.
    63	
    64	The construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring
    65	`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate
    66	spaces used in the dimension-extension argument of
    67	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293`.
    68	-/
    69	def AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : AdmissibleParams) : DirectLdParams where
    70	  q := P.q
    71	  m := 2 * P.m + 2
    72	  d := P.d
    73	  k := 1
    74	  hm := by omega
    75	  hd := P.hd
    76	  hk := by decide
    77	  hq := P.hq
    78	
    79	/-- A common random sample for the directly indexed question distribution.
    80	The point, coordinate index, and unrestricted direction are mutually uniform. -/
    81	structure DirectLdSpace (D : DirectLdParams) where
    82	  point : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    83	  index : Fin D.m
    84	  direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    85	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    86	
    87	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (DirectLdSpace D) :=
    88	  ⟨⟨0, D.firstIndex, 0⟩⟩
    89	
    90	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its point and the remaining independent
    91	coordinates. -/
    92	private def directLdSpacePointEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    93	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
    94	      (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
    95	        (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
    96	  toFun sample := (sample.point, sample.index, sample.direction)
    97	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.1, sample.2.1, sample.2.2⟩
    98	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
    99	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   100	
   101	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its stored index and the remaining
   102	independent coordinates. -/
   103	private def directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   104	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   105	      Fin D.m ×
   106	        ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
   107	          (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
   108	  toFun sample := (sample.index, sample.point, sample.direction)
   109	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.2.1, sample.1, sample.2.2⟩
   110	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   111	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   112	
   113	/-- Zero the coordinates preceding the directly sampled prefix index. -/
   114	def directPrefixProjection {D : DirectLdParams} (i : Fin D.m)
   115	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   116	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   117	
   118	/-- Canonical line descriptions whose coordinate index is stored directly.
   119	Coordinates are numbered from zero, so `index = i` represents coordinate
   120	`i + 1` in the paper. -/
   121	inductive DirectLineDesc (D : DirectLdParams) where
   122	  | axis (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   123	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection index) base = base)
   124	  | diagonal (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   125	      (direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
   126	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
   127	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < index.val → direction j = 0)
   128	  deriving DecidableEq
   129	
   130	/-- The kind of a directly indexed line. -/
   131	def DirectLineDesc.kind {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → LineKind
   132	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
   133	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
   134	
   135	/-- The coordinate index stored in a directly indexed line. -/
   136	def DirectLineDesc.index {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m
   137	  | .axis _ index _ => index
   138	  | .diagonal _ index _ _ _ => index
   139	
   140	/-- The canonical base point of a directly indexed line. -/
   141	def DirectLineDesc.base {D : DirectLdParams} :
   142	    DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
   143	  | .axis base _ _ => base
   144	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
   145	
   146	/-- The geometric direction of a directly indexed line. -/
   147	def DirectLineDesc.direction {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   148	    Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   149	  match line with
   150	  | .axis _ index _ => coordinateDirection index
   151	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
   152	
   153	/-- The base of a directly indexed description is fixed by its geometric
   154	direction. -/
   155	theorem DirectLineDesc.base_fixed {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   156	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
   157	  cases line with
   158	  | axis base index baseFixed => exact baseFixed
   159	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
   160	
   161	/-- Every directly indexed diagonal description retains its prefix-zero
   162	invariant. -/
   163	theorem DirectLineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {D : DirectLdParams}
   164	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
   165	    ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < line.index.val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   166	  cases line with
   167	  | axis base index baseFixed => simp [DirectLineDesc.kind] at hline
   168	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   169	
   170	/-- The point set represented by a directly indexed line. -/
   171	noncomputable def DirectLineDesc.pointSet {D : DirectLdParams}
   172	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) : Set (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :=
   173	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   174	
   175	/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical axis-line description. -/
   176	noncomputable def directALineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   177	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=
   178	  let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
   179	  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point
   180	  .axis base sample.index (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point)

     4	/-!
     5	# The directly indexed low-degree game
     6	
     7	This module defines polynomial evaluation, questions, answers, and the game
     8	for the directly indexed low-degree interface.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    23	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
    28	direct scalar field. -/
    29	abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
    30	  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D
    31	
    32	/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
    33	and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
    34	keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
    35	def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)
    36	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    37	    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
    38	  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    39	    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
    40	      evalCoefficient f t = a
    41	
    42	/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
    43	explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
    44	value is used as a fallback. -/
    45	noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    46	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    47	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    48	  classical
    49	  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    50	    some (Classical.choose h)
    51	  else none
    52	
    53	/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    54	abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D
    55	
    56	/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant
    57	coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and
    58	axis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/
    59	noncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :
    60	    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D
    61	  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
    62	  | .aline, sample =>
    63	      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
    64	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
    65	  | .dline, sample =>
    66	      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
    67	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform
    70	ordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample
    71	contains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/
    72	noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :
    73	    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=
    74	  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    75	    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
    76	      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))
    77	
    78	/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
    79	theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
    80	    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
    81	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability
    82	    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _
    83	
    84	/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    85	inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where
    86	  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
    87	  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    88	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    89	  deriving DecidableEq
    90	
    91	/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/
    92	abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
    93	  (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    94	    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    95	      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))
    96	
    97	/-- Constructor-preserving equivalence between the inductive answer type and
    98	its finite code. -/
    99	noncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   100	    DirectLdAnswer D ≃ DirectLdAnswerCode D where
   101	  toFun
   102	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   103	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   104	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   105	  invFun
   106	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   107	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   108	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   109	  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl
   110	  right_inv := by
   111	    intro answer
   112	    rcases answer with a | a
   113	    · rfl
   114	    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl
   115	
   116	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Inhabited (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   117	  ⟨.pointVals 0⟩
   118	
   119	noncomputable instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Fintype (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   120	  Fintype.ofEquiv (DirectLdAnswerCode D) (directLdAnswerEquiv D).symm
   121	
   122	/-- Check that a direct-game answer has the constructor required by its
   123	question type. -/
   124	def validDirectLdAnswer {D : DirectLdParams} (t : LdType)
   125	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) : Bool :=
   126	  match t, answer with
   127	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   128	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   129	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   130	  | _, _ => false
   131	
   132	/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   133	def directAlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   134	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   135	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   136	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   137	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   138	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection line.index →
   139	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   140	
   141	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   142	def directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   144	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   145	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   146	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   147	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   148	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   149	
   150	/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
   151	`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
   152	question. -/
   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false
   173	
   174	/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.
   175	It is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game
   176	`ldGame`. -/
   177	noncomputable def directLdGame (D : DirectLdParams) : Game where
   178	  QuestionA := DirectLdQuestion D
   179	  QuestionB := DirectLdQuestion D
   180	  AnswerA := DirectLdAnswer D
   181	  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D
   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D
   183	  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
   184	  decide := directLdWinPredicate D
   185	
   186	/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/
   187	def directLdPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   188	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   189	  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   190	
   191	/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.
   192	Wrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for
   193	`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/
   194	def directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   195	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D
   196	  | .pointVals values => values
   197	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   198	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   199	
   200	/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed
   201	game. -/
   202	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : DirectLdParams) :=
   203	  Fin D.k → PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d
   204	
   205	/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/
   206	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)
   207	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   208	  Measurement (DirectPolyTuple D) ι
   209	
   210	/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   211	def evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : DirectLdParams}
   212	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :
   213	    Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=
   214	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   215	
   216	end
   217	
   218	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree.Game
     2	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.DistributionAvg
