   253	/-- A mature `j`-restricted diagonal direction decodes to a direct direction
   254	vanishing before index `Fin.rev j`: the suffix restriction of the mature
   255	test is the prefix restriction of the direct game. -/
   256	theorem ldtPointToDirect_extendRestrictedDirection_prefix_zero
   257	    (D : DirectLdParams) (j : Fin D.m)
   258	    (free : Fin (j.val + 1) → Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   259	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   260	    ∀ c : Fin D.m, c.val < (Fin.rev j).val →
   261	      ldtPointToDirect D (extendRestrictedDirection j free) c = 0 := by
   262	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   263	  intro c hc
   264	  have hj := j.isLt
   265	  have hgt : ¬ (Fin.rev c).val ≤ j.val := by
   266	    rw [Fin.val_rev] at hc ⊢
   267	    omega
   268	  simp only [ldtPointToDirect, directPointEquiv_symm_apply,
   269	    extendRestrictedDirection, dif_neg hgt]
   270	  exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q)).symm_apply_apply 0

   272	/-- The leading index of a decoded `j`-restricted direction is `Fin.rev j`
   273	exactly on the generic event that its pivot coordinate `j` is nonzero. -/
   274	theorem directDiagonalIndexOf_extendRestrictedDirection
   275	    (D : DirectLdParams) (j : Fin D.m)
   276	    (free : Fin (j.val + 1) → Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   277	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   278	    free ⟨j.val, Nat.lt_succ_self _⟩ ≠ zeroCoord →
   279	      directDiagonalIndexOf D
   280	          (ldtPointToDirect D (extendRestrictedDirection j free)) =
   281	        Fin.rev j := by
   282	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   283	  intro hpivot
   284	  apply directDiagonalIndexOf_eq
   285	  · exact ldtPointToDirect_extendRestrictedDirection_prefix_zero D j free
   286	  · simp only [ldtPointToDirect, directPointEquiv_symm_apply, Fin.rev_rev,
   287	      extendRestrictedDirection, dif_pos (le_refl j.val)]
   288	    intro h
   289	    apply hpivot
   290	    have hcoded := congrArg (directScalarEquiv D) h
   291	    rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply] at hcoded
   292	    exact hcoded

   296	/-- Decoding an axis-line rebase is translation by the decoded scalar along
   297	the reversed direct coordinate direction. -/
   298	theorem ldtPointToDirect_axis_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   299	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters)
   300	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   301	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   302	    ldtPointToDirect D (line.rebaseAt t).base =
   303	      ldtPointToDirect D line.base +
   304	        (directScalarEquiv D).symm t •
   305	          coordinateDirection (Fin.rev line.direction) := by
   306	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   307	  funext i
   308	  simp only [ldtPointToDirect, directPointEquiv_symm_apply,
   309	    AxisParallelLine.rebaseAt, AxisParallelLine.pointAt, Pi.add_apply,
   310	    Pi.smul_apply]
   311	  by_cases hi : i = Fin.rev line.direction
   312	  · subst hi
   313	    simp only [coordinateDirection, Fin.rev_rev, if_pos, smul_eq_mul]
   314	    rw [Pi.single_eq_same, mul_one]
   315	    exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q)).symm_apply_apply _
   316	  · have hrev : Fin.rev i ≠ line.direction := by
   317	      intro h
   318	      apply hi
   319	      rw [← h, Fin.rev_rev]
   320	    simp [hi, hrev, coordinateDirection]

   322	/-- Decoding a diagonal-line rebase is translation by the decoded scalar
   323	along the decoded direct direction. -/
   324	theorem ldtPointToDirect_diagonal_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   325	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters)
   326	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   327	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   328	    ldtPointToDirect D (line.rebaseAt t).base =
   329	      ldtPointToDirect D line.base +
   330	        (directScalarEquiv D).symm t • ldtPointToDirect D line.direction := by
   331	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   332	  funext i
   333	  change decodeScalar
   334	      (addCoord (line.base (Fin.rev i))
   335	        (mulCoord t (line.direction (Fin.rev i)))) =
   336	    decodeScalar (line.base (Fin.rev i)) +
   337	      decodeScalar t * decodeScalar (line.direction (Fin.rev i))
   338	  simp [addCoord, mulCoord]

   340	/-- Canonical direct axis questions do not depend on the chosen base point of
   341	the mature line. -/
   342	theorem directAxisQuestionOf_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   343	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters)
   344	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   345	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   346	    directAxisQuestionOf D (line.rebaseAt t) = directAxisQuestionOf D line := by
   347	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel

   349	  rw [ldtPointToDirect_axis_rebase, lineRepMap_add_smul]

   351	/-- Canonical direct diagonal questions do not depend on the chosen base point
   352	of the mature line; the leading index depends only on the direction. -/
   353	theorem directDiagonalQuestionOf_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   354	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters)

   356	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   357	    directDiagonalQuestionOf D (line.rebaseAt t) =
   358	      directDiagonalQuestionOf D line := by
   359	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   360	  simp only [directDiagonalQuestionOf, DiagonalLine.rebaseAt]
   361	  have hrebase := ldtPointToDirect_diagonal_rebase D line t
   362	  change ldtPointToDirect D (line.pointAt t) =
   363	      ldtPointToDirect D line.base +
   364	        (directScalarEquiv D).symm t • ldtPointToDirect D line.direction at hrebase

   367	/-- The fixed scalar coding transports field addition to mature coordinate
   368	addition. -/

   370	    (x y : DirectScalarQ D) :
   371	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel

   404	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel

   428	/-- The constant diagonal-line answer with the given direct value. -/
   429	noncomputable def constantDiagonalAnswer (D : DirectLdParams)
   430	    (x : DirectScalarQ D) :
   431	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   432	    DiagonalLinePolynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
   433	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel

   437	/-- Constant answers are fixed by every reparametrization. -/
   438	theorem constantDiagonalAnswer_reparamAt (D : DirectLdParams)
   439	    (x : DirectScalarQ D) (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   440	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   441	    DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt (constantDiagonalAnswer D x) t =
   442	      constantDiagonalAnswer D x := by

   444	  apply DiagonalLinePolynomial.ext
   445	  simp [constantDiagonalAnswer, DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt]

   447	/-- A constant answer evaluates to its value at every parameter. -/
   448	theorem constantDiagonalAnswer_apply (D : DirectLdParams)
   449	    (x : DirectScalarQ D) (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   450	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   451	    constantDiagonalAnswer D x t = directScalarEquiv D x := by
   452	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   453	  change encodeScalar ((Polynomial.C x).eval (decodeScalar t)) =
   454	    directScalarEquiv D x

   458	/-- Read one simultaneous coordinate from a direct point answer. -/
   459	noncomputable def directPointAnswerReadout (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k) :
   460	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   461	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fq D.toLDTParameters := by
   462	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   463	  intro answer
   464	  exact match answer with
   465	    | .pointVals a => directScalarEquiv D (a r)
   466	    | .alinePolys _ => directScalarEquiv D 0
   467	    | .dlinePolys _ => directScalarEquiv D 0

   469	/-- Read one simultaneous coordinate from a direct axis-line answer and
   470	rebase its polynomial from the canonical direct line to the mature line. -/
   471	noncomputable def directAxisAnswerReadout (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   472	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters) :
   473	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   474	    DirectLdAnswer D → AxisLinePolynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
   475	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   476	  intro answer
   477	  exact match answer with
   478	    | .alinePolys a => AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt
   479	        (directAxisAnswerEquiv D (a r))
   480	        (directScalarEquiv D (directAxisRebaseParameter D line))
   481	    | .pointVals _ => default
   482	    | .dlinePolys _ => default
   483	
   484	/-- Read one simultaneous coordinate from a direct diagonal-line answer.  For
   485	a nonzero direction the polynomial is rebased from the canonical direct line
   486	to the mature line.  A zero direction is the singleton line through its base,
   487	where the direct predicate accepts an answer exactly when its polynomial
   488	function is constant with the point's value (`rem:ld-win-zero-direction`);
   489	the answer is read as the constant polynomial carrying its value at the base
   490	point, which is fixed by every reparametrization.  Wrong-form answers are
   491	sent to the default polynomial. -/
   492	noncomputable def directDiagonalAnswerReadout (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   493	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters) :
   494	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   495	    DirectLdAnswer D → DiagonalLinePolynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
   496	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   497	  classical
   498	  intro answer
   499	  exact match answer with
   500	    | .dlinePolys a =>
   501	        if ldtPointToDirect D line.direction = 0 then
   502	          constantDiagonalAnswer D (evalCoefficient (a r) 0)
   503	        else
   504	          DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt (directDiagonalAnswerEquiv D (a r))
   505	            (directScalarEquiv D (directDiagonalRebaseParameter D line))
   506	    | .pointVals _ => default
   507	    | .alinePolys _ => default

   509	/-- Axis answer readout is covariant under mature line rebasing. -/
   510	theorem directAxisAnswerReadout_rebase (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   511	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters)
   512	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) :
   513	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   514	    directAxisAnswerReadout D r (line.rebaseAt t) answer =
   515	      AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt (directAxisAnswerReadout D r line answer) t := by
   516	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   517	  cases answer with
   518	  | pointVals a => simp [directAxisAnswerReadout]
   519	  | dlinePolys a => simp [directAxisAnswerReadout]
   520	  | alinePolys a =>
   521	      simp only [directAxisAnswerReadout]
   522	      rw [directAxisRebaseParameter_rebase, directScalarEquiv_add]
   523	      rw [(directScalarEquiv D).apply_symm_apply]
   524	      exact (AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt_reparamAt
   525	        (directAxisAnswerEquiv D (a r)) _ _).symm
   526	
   527	/-- Diagonal answer readout is covariant under mature line rebasing, including
   528	the constant zero-direction convention. -/
   529	theorem directDiagonalAnswerReadout_rebase (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   530	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters)
   531	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) :
   532	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   533	    directDiagonalAnswerReadout D r (line.rebaseAt t) answer =
   534	      DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt
   535	        (directDiagonalAnswerReadout D r line answer) t := by
   536	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   537	  cases answer with
   538	  | pointVals a => simp [directDiagonalAnswerReadout]
   539	  | alinePolys a => simp [directDiagonalAnswerReadout]
   540	  | dlinePolys a =>
   541	      by_cases hdir : ldtPointToDirect D line.direction = 0
   542	      · have hrebase : ldtPointToDirect D (line.rebaseAt t).direction = 0 := by
   543	          simpa [DiagonalLine.rebaseAt] using hdir
   544	        simp [directDiagonalAnswerReadout, hdir, hrebase,
   545	          constantDiagonalAnswer_reparamAt]
   546	      · have hrebase : ldtPointToDirect D (line.rebaseAt t).direction ≠ 0 := by
   547	          simpa [DiagonalLine.rebaseAt] using hdir
   548	        simp only [directDiagonalAnswerReadout, hdir, hrebase, ↓reduceIte]
   549	        rw [directDiagonalRebaseParameter_rebase D line t hdir,
   550	          directScalarEquiv_add, (directScalarEquiv D).apply_symm_apply]
   551	        exact (DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt_reparamAt
   552	          (directDiagonalAnswerEquiv D (a r)) _ _).symm
   553

   218	theorem LdParams.seedFiberCard_pos (L : LdParams) : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   219	  exact Nat.div_pos (Nat.le_of_dvd (by
   220	    obtain ⟨n, hn, hq⟩ := L.hq
   221	    rw [hq]
   222	    exact Nat.pow_pos (by decide)) L.hdvd) L.hm

   225	index cardinality and the common fiber cardinality. -/
   226	theorem LdParams.seedFiberProduct_eq (L : LdParams) :

   230	/-- Casting between equal finite cardinalities preserves the underlying
   231	natural-number representative. -/
   232	@[simp] private theorem equivCastFin_val {m n : ℕ} (h : m = n) (i : Fin m) :
   233	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin h) i).val = i.val := by
   234	  subst n
   235	  rfl

   238	`chiIndex` fiber. -/
   239	noncomputable def seedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   240	    ScalarQ L ≃ Fin L.m × Fin (L.q / L.m) :=
   241	  (binaryRepresentation L.model).trans <|

   245	@[simp] theorem seedFiberEquiv_fst (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) :
   246	    (seedFiberEquiv L s).1 = chiIndex L s := by
   247	  letI : NeZero L.m := ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm)⟩
   248	  have hquot : (binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   249	    apply (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul L.seedFiberCard_pos).mpr
   250	    rw [Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd]
   251	    exact (binaryRepresentation L.model s).isLt
   252	  simp only [seedFiberEquiv, Equiv.trans_apply]
   253	  apply Fin.ext
   254	  change
   255	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq)
   256	      (binaryRepresentation L.model s)).val / (L.q / L.m) =
   257	      (Fin.ofNat L.m ((binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m))).val
   258	  rw [equivCastFin_val]
   259	  · exact (Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hquot).symm
   260	  · exact L.seedFiberProduct_eq

   334	/-- The ambient seed-indexed sample space is a direct sample together with a
   335	uniform residue in the selected seed fiber. -/
   336	noncomputable def ldSpaceSeedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   337	    LdSpace L ≃ DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams × Fin (L.q / L.m) where
   338	  toFun z :=
   339	    (⟨z.point, (seedFiberEquiv L z.seed).1, z.direction⟩,
   340	      (seedFiberEquiv L z.seed).2)
   341	  invFun x := ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L x.1 x.2
   342	  left_inv z := by
   343	    funext i
   344	    rcases i with (i | i)
   345	    · rcases i with (i | i)
   346	      · rfl
   347	      · rcases i with ⟨⟩
   348	        change (seedFiberEquiv L).symm (seedFiberEquiv L z.seed) = z.seed
   349	        exact (seedFiberEquiv L).symm_apply_apply z.seed
   350	    · rfl
   351	  right_inv x := by
   352	    rcases x with ⟨sample, residue⟩
   353	    apply Prod.ext
   354	    · cases sample with
   355	      | mk point index direction =>
   356	          simp only [ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_point,
   357	            ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_seed, ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_direction]
   358	          rw [seedFiberEquiv_seedOfIndexResidue]

   403	noncomputable def ldQuestionSeedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :

   436	  let residue := (ldSpaceSeedFiberEquiv L source.2).2
   437	  have hsource :

   439	    exact (ldSpaceSeedFiberEquiv L).symm_apply_apply source.2 |>.symm

   447	theorem ldQuestionDistribution_map_parse (L : LdParams) :

   450	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=

   452	  let sourceMap : ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace L) →

   459	          DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams := fun source =>
   460	    ((source.1.1, directLdMap L.toDirectLdParams source.1.1 source.2),

1	\section{The test}\label{sec:the-test}
     2	
     3	\begin{definition}[Roles]
     4	The low individual degree test will be played between two provers and a verifier.
     5	The two provers are named Player~$\mathrm{A}$ and Player~$\mathrm{B}$.
     6	A \emph{role} $r$ is an element of the set $\{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$.
     7	Given a role~$r$, we write $\overline{r}$ for the other element of the set $\{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$.
     8	\end{definition}
     9	
    10	\begin{definition}[Low individual degree test]
    11	Let~$m$ and~$d$ be nonnegative integers.
    12	Let $q$ be a prime power.
    13	Then the \emph{$(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test}
    14	is stated in \Cref{fig:test}.
    15	\end{definition}
    16	
    17	{
    18	\floatstyle{boxed} 
    19	\restylefloat{figure}
    20	\begin{figure}
    21	With probability~$\tfrac{1}{3}$ each, perform one of the following three tests.
    22	\begin{enumerate}
    23		\item \textbf{Axis-parallel lines test:}
    24			Pick a uniformly random role $\br \sim \{\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B}\}$.
    25			Let $\bu \sim \F_q^m$ be a uniformly random point.
    26			Select $\bi \sim \{1, \ldots, m\}$ uniformly at random,

    71	An important class of strategies are those which are \emph{symmetric}.
    72	In this case, the bipartite state $\ket{\psi}$ Alice and Bob share is symmetric.
    73	Furthermore, for any question Alice and Bob receive, they apply the same measurement to their share of the state.
    74	This means that rather than, for example, keeping track of a separate points measurement for Alice and Bob,
    75	we can use a single measurement to refer to both of their strategies,
    76	and similarly for the axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines measurements.
    77	This is formalized in the following definition, where we also consider strategies which are projective.
    78	
    79	\begin{definition}[Symmetric, projective strategy]
    80	A \emph{symmetric, projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test
    81	is a tuple $(\psi, A, B, L)$ defined as follows.
    82	\begin{itemize}
    83	\item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \calH \ot \calH$ is a bipartite, permutation-invariant state.
    84	\item[$\circ$] $A = \{A^u_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \F_q^m$ and $a \in \F_q$.
    85				For each $u$, $A^u$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    86	\item[$\circ$] $B = \{B^{\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
    87				and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
    88				For each $\ell$, $B^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    89	\item[$\circ$] $L = \{L^{\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
    90				and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
    91				For each $\ell$, $L^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    92	\end{itemize}
    93	\end{definition}
    94	
    95	We can also consider more general strategies which are no longer assumed to be symmetric.
    96	In this case, Players~$\mathrm{A}$ and~$\mathrm{B}$ each have their own versions of the measurements~$A$, $B$, and~$L$.
    97	
    98	\begin{definition}[General projective strategy]
    99	A \emph{projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test
   100	is a tuple $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ defined as follows.
   101	\begin{itemize}
   102	\item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$ is a bipartite state.
   103	\end{itemize}
   104	Furthermore, for each~$w \in \{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$:
   105	\begin{itemize}
   106	\item[$\circ$] $A^{w} = \{A^{w,u}_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \F_q^m$ and $a \in \F_q$.
   107				For each $u$, $A^{w,u}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   108	\item[$\circ$] $B^{w} = \{B^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
   109				and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
   110				For each $\ell$, $B^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   111	\item[$\circ$] $L^w = \{L^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$

   113				For each $\ell$, $L^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.

   115	\end{definition}

\section{Candidate repairs}

\paragraph{Direct index sampling (candidate direction, recommended).}
Define, for arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the line-point distribution over
$\F_q^{m'}$ that samples the uniform point, the uniform axis index
$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
$i-1$ coordinates, directly; define the \emph{directly indexed game} with
this question distribution, whose line questions carry the index $i$ (and,
for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place of the seed
$s \in \F_q$; and state the imported soundness theorem for that game
(form~4 above).  This removes the divisibility obstruction and nothing
else: the directly indexed game still asks for polynomials on revealed
lines, has no pair questions, and weighs its branches as the present game
does, so establishing form~4 carries the same two import obligations as
the $\chi$-based import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), now at
arbitrary dimension.

The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must moreover be proved
at the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the
two games have different question alphabets: an $\mathsf{ALine}$ question
of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\mathsf{DLine}$
question a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different
measurements for seeds $s \ne s'$ with $\chi(s) = \chi(s')$, and equality
of the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport
such a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following
obligations, none of which is carried out here.
\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \mid q$, the image of the
  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map
  $(u_0,s) \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s),v')$
  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the
  seed is uniform on the class $\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything
  else.
  \item \emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game
  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the
  $\chi$-based game.  Since the win predicate depends on the question only
  through the parsed data, and a seed-oblivious strategy answers
  identically across each fiber --- in particular on the synchronicity
  branches, where both players hold the same seed --- the value should be
  preserved exactly on every branch, and projectivity is preserved.  This
  is the direction the combining subtree needs.
  \item \emph{Seed-fiber averaging: what it preserves and what it does
  not.}  In the opposite direction, average each line measurement over its
  seed fiber: attach to a direct question $(u_0,i)$, respectively
  $(u_0,i,v')$, the average over uniform $s \in \chi^{-1}(i)$ of the
  measurements attached to $(u_0,s)$, respectively $(u_0,s,v')$, leaving
  the points measurements unchanged.  By the conditional uniformity of the
  seed this preserves the value of every \emph{line-versus-point} branch
  exactly: there the paired question carries no seed, so the branch value
  is an average over the fiber of per-seed values, which the averaged
  measurement computes.  It does \emph{not} preserve the synchronicity
  branches.  There both players hold the same seed, so the $\chi$-based
  branch value is the diagonal average
  $\E_{s}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s)}_f
  \rangle$, while the averaged strategy realizes the double average
  $\E_{s,s'}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s')}_f
  \rangle$ over independent seeds in the fiber; the two differ whenever
  the players' measurements vary across a fiber in a correlated way (if
  both apply a common seed-dependent relabelling, every diagonal term is
  large and the cross terms are not), and neither quantity dominates the
  other in general.  An earlier revision of this note claimed that the
  averaging preserves the exact value, and with it synchronicity; that
  claim was wrong and is withdrawn.  What needs proof is control of the
  synchronicity branches under de-seeding.  Candidate approaches: show
  that a strategy of value $1-\eps$ in the $\chi$-based game is, with
  polynomial loss, close to a seed-oblivious one; or state form~4 with a
  synchronicity hypothesis in the doubled-average form and re-derive it on
  the tensor-code side.  Choosing and proving one of these is an open
  obligation.
  \item \emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM
  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported
  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The
  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one
  (Naimark preserves all product correlations
  $\langle X \ot Y \rangle$ of the given strategy against the dilated
  state --- hence the value of every branch the averaging preserved ---
  but nothing restores the diagonal seed correlations once the averaging
  has been performed); apply form~4; and compress the resulting polynomial
  measurement along the dilation isometry back to a POVM in the required
  measurement class on the original space.  That this compression
  preserves the consistency conclusions must itself be proved; it is
  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4
  may be stated for POVM strategies outright, moving the dilation inside
  the import.)

def duplicateDeclarations (cfg : Target) : CoreM (Array (Array Name)) := MetaM.run' do
  let env ← getEnv
  let mut visited : Std.HashMap Expr Name := {}
  let mut dups : Std.HashMap Expr (Array Name) := {}
  for (name, cinfo) in env.constants.map₁ do
    if name.isInternalDetail
      || name.isMetaprogramming

      || Linter.isDeprecated env name
      || isAlias cinfo then continue
    if ← isProp cinfo.type then
      unless cfg matches .theorems do continue
    else
      match cfg with
      | .theorems => continue
      | .instances => if (← isClass? cinfo.type).isNone then continue

    97	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    98	-/
    99	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=

   103	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

   105	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=

   108	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   109	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   110	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   112	-/
   113	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   114	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   115	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   116	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   117	
   118	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   119	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   120	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   121	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   122	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   123	-/
   124	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   125	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   126	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   127	
   128	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   129	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   130	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   132	-/
   133	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   134	  fun i => match i with
   135	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   136	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   137	  | .inr _ => 0
   138	
   139	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   140	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   141	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   142	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   143	-/
   144	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   145	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   146	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   147	  fun i => match i with
   148	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   149	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   150	  | .inr _ => 0
   151	
   152	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   153	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   154	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   155	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   156	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   157	-/
   158	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   159	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   160	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   161	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   162	  fun i => match i with
   163	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   164	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   165	  | .inr j => direction j

   195	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   196	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   197	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   198	-/
   199	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   200	
   201	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   202	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   203	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   204	-/
   205	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   206	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   207	  Distribution.map
   208	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   209	    (fun s =>
   210	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   211	
   212	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   213	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   214	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   215	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   216	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   217	-/
   218	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   219	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   220	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   221	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   222	  deriving DecidableEq
   223	
   224	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   225	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   226	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   227	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   228	-/
   229	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   230	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   231	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   232	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   233	
   234	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   235	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   236	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   237	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   238	-/
   239	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   240	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   241	  toFun
   242	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   243	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   244	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   245	  invFun
   246	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   247	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   248	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   249	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   250	  right_inv := by
   251	    intro x
   252	    cases x with
   253	    | inl a => rfl
   254	    | inr x =>
   255	        cases x with
   256	        | inl a => rfl
   257	        | inr a => rfl
   258	
   259	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   260	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   261	
   262	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   263	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   264	
   265	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   266	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   267	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   268	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   269	-/
   270	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   271	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   272	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   273	
   274	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   275	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   276	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   277	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   278	-/
   279	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   280	  match t, a with
   281	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   282	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   283	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   284	  | _, _ => false
   285	
   286	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   287	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   288	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   289	-/
   290	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   291	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   292	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   293	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   294	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   295	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   296	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   297	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   298	
   299	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   301	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   302	-/
   303	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   304	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   305	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   306	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   307	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   308	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   309	
   310	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   311	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   312	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   313	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   314	-/
   315	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   316	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   317	  open Classical in
   318	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   319	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   320	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   321	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   322	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   323	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   324	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   325	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   327	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   328	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   329	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   330	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   331	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   332	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   333	      else false
   334	
   335	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   336	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   337	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   338	-/
   339	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   340	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   341	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   342	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   343	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   344	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   345	  μ_prob := by sorry
   346	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   347	
   348	end
   349	
   350	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

Shared distribution definitions: finite-support weighted distributions,

/-- A finite-support weighted distribution with nonnegative real-valued weights. -/
structure Distribution (α : Type*) where
  support : Finset α := ∅
  weight : α → Error := fun _ => 0
  nonnegative : ∀ a, 0 ≤ weight a := by intro _; positivity
  outsideSupport : ∀ a, a ∉ support → weight a = 0 := by intro _ _; rfl

namespace Distribution

/-- The total mass carried by the explicit support of a distribution. -/
def totalWeight {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Error :=
  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a

/-- A `Distribution` is probabilistic when its total mass is exactly `1`. -/
def IsProbability {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Prop :=
  𝒟.totalWeight = 1

abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=

/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)

      evalCoefficient f t = a

1	# MIPStarRE-local convention addenda
     2	
     3	The canonical convention documents live in the `lean-conventions` skill of
     4	[texra-ai/texra-lean-skills](https://github.com/texra-ai/texra-lean-skills)
     5	(auto-installed for Claude Code sessions via `.claude/settings.json`; other
     6	agents: clone the repository and symlink the skill directories, per its
     7	README). This file holds only
     8	MIPStarRE's project-local facts — it restates no shared rule, and shared
     9	rules never move here.
    10	
    11	## Style (MATHLIB_style)
    12	
    13	### Linter warnings
    14	
    15	Do not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. A cleanup PR should not add
    16	broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks, and especially not file-wide
    17	blocks, just to make the build output quieter. Linters exist to expose real
    18	maintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.
    19	
    20	Fix the warning at its source whenever possible:
    21	
    22	- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;
    23	- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass
    24	  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;
    25	- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;
    26	- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than
    27	  silencing `linter.flexible`.
    28	
    29	If a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting
    30	exception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably
    31	`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.
    32	Such exceptions should be rare and reviewable. Never use linter suppression as
    33	the main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.
    34	
    35	## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)
    36	
    37	### Source-faithfulness checks
    38	
    39	For this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean
    40	statement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`.  Before
    41	applying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions
    42	`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed
    43	source-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the
    44	corresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.
    45	
    46	Reject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,
    47	repair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,
    48	or arbitrary implication hypothesis.  Necessary boundary hypotheses, such as
    49	positivity for division or nonemptiness of a finite type, may be faithful formal
    50	encodings of implicit paper assumptions, but they should be documented when
    51	mathematically load-bearing.
    52	
    53	Reviewers should also inspect `\lean{}` and `\leanok` links.  A source-labelled
    54	blueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction
    55	theorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.
    56	Auxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the
    57	remark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.
    58	
    59	## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)
    60	
    61	### Companion document
    62	
    63	> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues
    64	> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the
    65	> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still
    66	> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,
    67	> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default
    68	> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).
    69	> Consult it alongside this file during review.
    70	
    71	### Project paper-realignment protocol
    72	
    73	The canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions
    74	`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as
    75	follows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in
    76	`AGENTS.md`):
    77	
    78	> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a
    79	> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`
    80	> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be
    81	> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The
    82	> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof
    83	> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the
    84	> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a
    85	> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or
    86	> conditional helper
    87	> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.
    88	> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge
    89	> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.
    90	
    91	### Axiom policy
    92	
    93	When an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,
    94	prefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`
    95	declaration, and add a regression check (for example a
    96	`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in
    97	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen
    98	the axiomatic base.
    99	
   100	This preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper
   101	theorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a
   102	caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a
   103	proof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly
   104	conditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement
   105	faithful to the paper.
   106	
   107	### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization
   108	
   109	This is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or
   110	theorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,
   111	making them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.
   112	
   113	Signs to watch for:
   114	
   115	- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,
   116	  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's
   117	  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)
   118	- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types
   119	  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions
   120	- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical
   121	  semantics (e.g., a "projective measurement" definition that does not enforce
   122	  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)
   123	- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be
   124	  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything
   125	- Definitions that "work" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to
   126	  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,
   127	  incompatible universes)
   128	
   129	When reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of
   130	this?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the
   131	scaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks
   132	progress rather than enabling it.
   133	
   134	### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift
   135	
   136	A theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker
   137	if its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.
   138	Changing a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is
   139	strongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a
   140	documented mathematical necessity.
   141	
   142	The most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an
   143	extra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional
   144	theorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not
   145	repair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named
   146	`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,
   147	generic `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those
   148	assumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.
   149	
   150	Conditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet
   151	be closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a
   152	named lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional
   153	helper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named
   154	obligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show
   155	that it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or
   156	`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled
   157	blueprint theorem with `\leanok`.
   158	
   159	Existing bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs
   160	for reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a
   161	strengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the
   162	bridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is
   163	to restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a
   164	tracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.
   165	
   166	Not every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed
   167	to encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model
   168	instances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be
   169	faithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These
   170	conditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is
   171	mathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate
   172	step of the source proof.
   173	
   174	For every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:
   175	
   176	- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;
   177	- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;
   178	- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened
   179	  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.
   180	
   181	### Source-statement proof gaps
   182	
   183	**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read
   184	[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a
   185	proof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation
   186	structure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why
   187	conditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a
   188	tracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.
   360	---
   361	
   362	## 5. Review Checklist
   363	
   364	Every PR touching Lean code should be reviewed against these criteria:
   365	
   366	1. **Proof correctness** -- No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.
   367	   Run `rg -n "sorry|axiom" <file>` to verify.
   368

   155	@[simp] theorem roleRegisterProjMeas_A_B {Outcome ιA ιB : Type*}
   156	    [Inhabited Outcome] [Fintype Outcome]
   157	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]

   168	    (roleRegisterProjMeas MA MB).outcome a (Role.B, i) (Role.A, j) = 0 :=

     4	/-!
     5	# The directly indexed low-degree game
     6	
     7	This module defines polynomial evaluation, questions, answers, and the game
     8	for the directly indexed low-degree interface.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    23	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
    28	direct scalar field. -/
    29	abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
    30	  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D
    31	
    32	/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
    33	and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
    34	keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
    35	def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)
    36	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    37	    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
    38	  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    39	    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
    40	      evalCoefficient f t = a
    41	
    42	/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
    43	explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
    44	value is used as a fallback. -/
    45	noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    46	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    47	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    48	  classical
    49	  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    50	    some (Classical.choose h)
    51	  else none
    52	
    53	/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    54	abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D
    55	
    56	/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant
    57	coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and
    58	axis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/
    59	noncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :
    60	    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D
    61	  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
    62	  | .aline, sample =>
    63	      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
    64	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
    65	  | .dline, sample =>
    66	      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
    67	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform
    70	ordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample
    71	contains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/
    72	noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :
    73	    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=
    74	  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    75	    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
    76	      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))
    77	
    78	/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
    79	theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
    80	    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
    81	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability
    82	    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _
    83	
    84	/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    85	inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where
    86	  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
    87	  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    88	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    89	  deriving DecidableEq
    90	
    91	/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/
    92	abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
    93	  (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    94	    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    95	      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))
    96	
    97	/-- Constructor-preserving equivalence between the inductive answer type and
    98	its finite code. -/
    99	noncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   100	    DirectLdAnswer D ≃ DirectLdAnswerCode D where
   101	  toFun
   102	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   103	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   104	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   105	  invFun
   106	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   107	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   108	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   109	  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl
   110	  right_inv := by
   111	    intro answer
   112	    rcases answer with a | a
   113	    · rfl
   114	    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl
   115	
   116	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Inhabited (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   117	  ⟨.pointVals 0⟩
   118	
   119	noncomputable instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Fintype (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   120	  Fintype.ofEquiv (DirectLdAnswerCode D) (directLdAnswerEquiv D).symm
   121	
   122	/-- Check that a direct-game answer has the constructor required by its
   123	question type. -/
   124	def validDirectLdAnswer {D : DirectLdParams} (t : LdType)
   125	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) : Bool :=
   126	  match t, answer with
   127	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   128	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   129	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   130	  | _, _ => false
   131	
   132	/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   133	def directAlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   134	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   135	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   136	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   137	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   138	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection line.index →
   139	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   140	
   141	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   142	def directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   144	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   145	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   146	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   147	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   148	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   149	
   150	/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
   151	`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
   152	question. -/
   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false
   173	
   174	/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.
   175	It is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game
   176	`ldGame`. -/
   177	noncomputable def directLdGame (D : DirectLdParams) : Game where
   178	  QuestionA := DirectLdQuestion D
   179	  QuestionB := DirectLdQuestion D
   180	  AnswerA := DirectLdAnswer D
   181	  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D
   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D
   183	  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
   184	  decide := directLdWinPredicate D
   185	
   186	/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/
   187	def directLdPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   188	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   189	  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   190	
   191	/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.
   192	Wrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for
   193	`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/
   194	def directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   195	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D
   196	  | .pointVals values => values
   197	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   198	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   199	
   200	/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed
   201	game. -/
   202	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : DirectLdParams) :=
   203	  Fin D.k → PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d
   204	
   205	/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/
   206	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)
   207	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   208	  Measurement (DirectPolyTuple D) ι
   209	
   210	/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   211	def evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : DirectLdParams}
   212	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :
   213	    Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=
   214	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   215	
   216	end
   217	
   218	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree.Game
     2	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.DistributionAvg
     3	
     4	/-!
     5	# Rejection probabilities for the directly indexed low-degree game
     6	
     7	This module compares the rejection probability of the directly indexed game
     8	with the branch weights used by the mature low-individual-degree test.
     9	All declarations below are formalization-only support derived from the game
    10	value; none is a paper-labelled result.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The uniform distribution on the three ordered question types is specified in
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:178-186`,
    16	and its verifier is specified in the same file at lines 320-392.  The mature
    17	low-individual-degree test's three equal outer weights and its uniform role
    18	choices are specified in `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:10-67`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	private theorem directLdAccepted_add_rejected_eq_one
    31	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    32	    (types : LdType × LdType) (sample : DirectLdSpace D) :
    33	    (∑ a : (directLdGame D).AnswerA, ∑ b : (directLdGame D).AnswerB,
    34	        if directLdWinPredicate D
    35	            (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
    36	            (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample) a b then
    37	          outcomeWeight S
    38	            (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
    39	            (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample) a b
    40	        else 0) +
    41	      (∑ a : (directLdGame D).AnswerA, ∑ b : (directLdGame D).AnswerB,
    42	        if directLdWinPredicate D
    43	            (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
    44	            (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample) a b then
    45	          0
    46	        else outcomeWeight S
    47	          (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
    48	          (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample) a b) = 1 := by
    49	  calc
    50	    _ = ∑ a : (directLdGame D).AnswerA, ∑ b : (directLdGame D).AnswerB,
    51	        outcomeWeight S
    52	          (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
    53	          (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample) a b := by
    54	      rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    55	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    56	      intro a _
    57	      rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    58	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    59	      intro b _
    60	      by_cases h : directLdWinPredicate D
    61	          (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
    62	          (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample) a b
    63	      · simp [h]
    64	      · simp [h]
    65	    _ = 1 := outcomeWeight_sum_eq_one S
    66	      (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
    67	      (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample)
    68	
    69	/-- Rejection probability conditioned on an ordered pair of low-degree
    70	question types, averaged over the common direct sample. -/
    71	noncomputable def directLdBranchRejectionProbability
    72	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    73	    (types : LdType × LdType) : ℝ :=
    74	  avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)) fun sample =>
    75	    ∑ a : (directLdGame D).AnswerA, ∑ b : (directLdGame D).AnswerB,
    76	      if directLdWinPredicate D
    77	          (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
    78	          (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample) a b then
    79	        0
    80	      else outcomeWeight S
    81	        (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
    82	        (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample) a b
    83	
    84	/-- Total rejection probability of the directly indexed low-degree game,
    85	averaged uniformly over its nine ordered type branches. -/
    86	noncomputable def directLdRejectionProbability
    87	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) : ℝ :=
    88	  avgOver (uniformDistribution (LdType × LdType))
    89	    (directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S)
    90	
    91	/-- The branch failure probability with the weights used by the mature
    92	low-individual-degree test. -/
    93	noncomputable def directLdLdtWeightedFailureProbability
    94	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) : ℝ :=
    95	  let B := directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S
    96	  ((B (.aline, .point) + B (.point, .aline)) / 2 +
    97	      B (.point, .point) +
    98	      (B (.dline, .point) + B (.point, .dline)) / 2) / 3
    99	
   100	private theorem sum_ldType (f : LdType → ℝ) :
   101	    ∑ t : LdType, f t = f .point + f .aline + f .dline := by
   102	  change (Finset.univ : Finset LdType).sum f = _
   103	  rw [show (Finset.univ : Finset LdType) = {.point, .aline, .dline} by decide]
   104	  simp [add_assoc]
   105	
   106	private theorem avgOver_ldType_pair (f : LdType × LdType → ℝ) :
   107	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (LdType × LdType)) f =
   108	      (f (.point, .point) + f (.point, .aline) + f (.point, .dline) +
   109	        (f (.aline, .point) + f (.aline, .aline) + f (.aline, .dline)) +
   110	        (f (.dline, .point) + f (.dline, .aline) + f (.dline, .dline))) / 9 := by
   111	  unfold avgOver uniformDistribution Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   112	  simp only [Finset.mem_univ, if_true, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_prod]
   113	  rw [show Fintype.card LdType = 3 by decide]
   114	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   115	  simp_rw [sum_ldType]
   116	  ring
   117	
   118	/-- Every fixed-type rejection probability is nonnegative. -/
   119	theorem directLdBranchRejectionProbability_nonneg
   120	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   121	    (types : LdType × LdType) :
   122	    0 ≤ directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S types := by
   123	  apply avgOver_nonneg
   124	  intro sample
   125	  apply Finset.sum_nonneg
   126	  intro a _
   127	  apply Finset.sum_nonneg
   128	  intro b _
   129	  by_cases h : directLdWinPredicate D
   130	      (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
   131	      (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample) a b
   132	  · simp [h]
   133	  · simpa [h] using outcomeWeight_nonneg S
   134	      (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
   135	      (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample) a b
   136	
   137	/-- Total direct-game rejection is one minus the strategy value. -/
   138	theorem directLdRejectionProbability_eq_one_sub_value
   139	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
   140	    directLdRejectionProbability D S = 1 - S.value := by
   141	  let accepted : (LdType × LdType) → DirectLdSpace D → ℝ :=
   142	    fun types sample =>
   143	      ∑ a : (directLdGame D).AnswerA, ∑ b : (directLdGame D).AnswerB,
   144	        if directLdWinPredicate D
   145	            (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
   146	            (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample) a b then
   147	          outcomeWeight S
   148	            (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 sample)
   149	            (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 sample) a b
   150	        else 0
   151	  have hbranch (types : LdType × LdType) :
   152	      directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S types =
   153	        1 - avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)) (accepted types) := by
   154	    rw [show directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S types =
   155	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D))
   156	          (fun sample => 1 - accepted types sample) by
   157	      apply avgOver_congr
   158	      intro sample
   159	      dsimp [accepted]
   160	      linarith [directLdAccepted_add_rejected_eq_one D S types sample]]
   161	    rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_uniform_const]
   162	  rw [show directLdRejectionProbability D S =
   163	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (LdType × LdType))
   164	        (fun types => 1 -
   165	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)) (accepted types)) by
   166	    unfold directLdRejectionProbability
   167	    apply avgOver_congr
   168	    exact hbranch]
   169	  rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_uniform_const]
   170	  congr 1
   171	  rw [Strategy.value]
   172	  symm
   173	  change avgOver (directLdQuestionDistribution D) _ = _
   174	  rw [directLdQuestionDistribution, Distribution.avgOver_map]
   175	  exact avgOver_uniform_prod (f := accepted)
   176	
   177	/-- The mature low-individual-degree branch weighting is at most three times
   178	the uniformly weighted direct-game rejection probability. -/
   179	theorem directLdLdtWeightedFailureProbability_le_three_mul_rejection
   180	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
   181	    directLdLdtWeightedFailureProbability D S ≤
   182	      3 * directLdRejectionProbability D S := by
   183	  have hnonneg := directLdBranchRejectionProbability_nonneg D S
   184	  have hpp := hnonneg (.point, .point)
   185	  have hpa := hnonneg (.point, .aline)
   186	  have hpd := hnonneg (.point, .dline)
   187	  have hap := hnonneg (.aline, .point)

    29	/-- Relabel a matrix measurement along an equivalence of outcome alphabets. -/
    30	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementTransport
    31	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    32	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    33	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
    34	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement beta iota :=
    35	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    36	    (fun b => M.effect (e.symm b))
    37	    (fun b => M.pos (e.symm b))
    38	    (by
    39	      calc
    40	        ∑ b, M.effect (e.symm b) = ∑ a, M.effect a :=
    41	          Equiv.sum_comp e.symm M.effect
    42	        _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one)
    43

    45	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    47	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    48	    (b : beta) :
    49	    (matrixMeasurementTransport e M).effect b = M.effect (e.symm b) :=
    50	  rfl

    52	/-- Relabeling a projective matrix measurement preserves projectivity. -/
    53	theorem matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
    54	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    55	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    56	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    57	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :

    61	/-- Assemble a family of matrix measurements as diagonal blocks indexed by a
    62	finite classical register. -/
    63	noncomputable def blockDiagonalMeasurement
    64	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
    65	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    66	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
    67	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
    68	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block) :=
    69	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    70	    (fun a => Matrix.blockDiagonal fun r => (M r).effect a)
    71	    (fun a => Matrix.blockDiagonal_nonneg
    72	      (fun r => (M r).effect a) (fun r => (M r).pos a))
    73	    (by
    74	      ext ⟨i, r⟩ ⟨j, s⟩
    75	      simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply]
    76	      by_cases hrs : r = s
    77	      · subst s
    78	        simp only [if_pos]
    79	        calc
    80	          ∑ x, (M r).effect x i j = (1 : Matrix iota iota ℂ) i j :=
    81	            by
    82	              simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using
    83	                congrFun (congrFun (M r).sum_eq_one i) j
    84	          _ = (1 : Matrix (iota × block) (iota × block) ℂ)
    85	              (i, r) (j, r) := by
    86	                change (if i = j then 1 else 0) =
    87	                  (if (i, r) = (j, r) then 1 else 0)
    88	                simp
    89	      · simp [hrs])

   143	/-- Reindexing Euclidean coordinates along an equivalence preserves norm. -/
   144	theorem reindexState_norm_eq
   145	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   146	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   147	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   148	    (e : iota ≃ kappa) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   149	    ‖reindexState e psi‖ = ‖psi‖ := by
   150	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)]
   151	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   152	  change (∑ j : kappa, ‖psi (e.symm j)‖ ^ 2) = ∑ i : iota, ‖psi i‖ ^ 2

   155	/-- The coordinate tensor of two Euclidean vectors has the product norm. -/
   156	theorem vecTensor_norm_eq
   157	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   158	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   159	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   160	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ kappa) :
   161	    ‖vecTensor u v‖ = ‖u‖ * ‖v‖ := by
   162	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _))]
   163	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, mul_pow, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq,

   165	  change (∑ p : iota × kappa, ‖u p.1 * v p.2‖ ^ 2) =
   166	    (∑ i : iota, ‖u i‖ ^ 2) * ∑ j : kappa, ‖v j‖ ^ 2

15:The classical low individual degree game is a two-player game based on the low individual degree variant of the multilinearity test of Babai, Fortnow, and Lund. In the basic version, one player (the ``points player'') receives a uniformly random point $u \in \F_q^m$ and answers with a value $a \in \F_q$, while the other player (the ``lines player'') receives a random line through $u$ --- either axis-parallel or diagonal --- and answers with a univariate polynomial describing the restriction of a global function to that line. If the players share a polynomial $g\colon \F_q^m \to \F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$ and answer with $g(u)$ and with the restriction $g|_\ell$, they win with probability $1$; the soundness theorem below states that the converse approximately holds. In the simultaneous version, the players' answers are $k$-tuples, checked coordinatewise against a $k$-tuple of low individual degree polynomials.

# Strategy transport for the directly indexed low-degree game

This module reads one coordinate of a projective directly indexed strategy as
a two-space mature low individual degree strategy.  The question and answer
transport of `Transport.Questions` supplies the canonical direct question of
every mature line, with the reversed coordinate order and the leading index
of the decoded diagonal direction, together with answer readouts that are
covariant under line rebasing; this establishes all four covariance
conditions of `ProjStrat`.  The module also records exact Born-weight
formulas for both directions of strategy transport.
